items.title: Kourittenga : La communauté musulmane du village de Zaogo célèbre le Maouloud 2026 sous le signe de la cohésion sociale
items.description: BURKINA-KOURITTENGA-MAOULOUD-COMMEMORATION Kourittenga : La communauté musulmane du village de Zaogo célèbre le Maouloud 2026 sous le signe de la cohésion sociale Koupéla, 26 août 2026 (AIB)- Les fidèles musulmans de Zaogo, dans la commune de Koupéla, ont célébré, dans la nuit du 25 au 26 août 2026, le Maouloud, marquant la naissance du prophète Mohamed, en présence des autorités coutumières et administratives du Kourittenga, conduites par le Haut-Commissaire de la province du Kourittenga, Moctar Ilboudo. Ils ont prié pour le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et les bonnes pratiques religieuses. Les fidèles musulmans du village de Zaogo ont célébré le Maouloud dans la nuit du 25 au 26 août 2026 et ont mis l'accent sur les fondements de l’islam, le renforcement de la cohésion sociale et la promotion des bonnes pratiques religieuses. Lecture du Coran, prières collectives et enseignements spirituels ont été dispensés tout au long de la nuit. Le président de la communauté musulmane de Zaogo, Cheick El Hadj Dawendé Haïdara a axé ses interventions sur la pratique religieuse, l'unité citoyenne et l'effort collectif. « Le Maouloud constitue un rappel des enseignements du Prophète Mohamed. Cette commémoration invite chaque fidèle à s'adapter aux valeurs fondamentales de l'islam, fondées sur la tolérance, la solidarité et la recherche de la paix», a-t-il indiqué. S'adressant aux autorités et aux citoyens venus participer aux prières, Cheick El Hadj Dawendé Haïdara a rappelé la nécessité de préserver le tissu social. « La cohésion sociale demeure le socle de notre vie communautaire. La présence des autorités administratives et coutumières à nos côtés traduit cette volonté commune de rassembler tous les fils et toutes les filles de la province autour des principes de vivre-ensemble », a-t-il dit. S’adressant aux musulmans, le président de la communauté musulmane de Zaogo a invité les acteurs de la vie locale à adopter des comportements conformes aux enseignements de l’islam et à œuvrer quotidiennement en faveur de la stabilité du pays. Il a particulièrement exhorté la jeunesse à s’investir davantage dans le travail et à accompagner les efforts collectifs en faveur du développement. La veillée s'est achevée par des invocations à l'attention des forces engagées sur le terrain et pour le rétablissement de la sécurité sur l'ensemble du territoire national. Agence d’information du Burkina AWS/HB/OO

items.title: 19 killed, 384 travellers missing in Nepal floods at China border; 'major casualties' reported in Tibet mudslide
items.description: Massive flooding near the border with Tibet killed at least 19 people in Nepal on Wednesday, but hundreds of tourists were still out of contact hours after the disaster hit. A torrent of mud and debris burst from the banks of a river between China and Nepal, burying buildings and triggering a frantic search for survivors. Chinese state media reported “major casualties” from a mudslide at a Tibet trade hub on China’s side of its border with Nepal, and President Xi Jinping ordered an “all-out” rescue effort. “I got a call from (my brother-in-law) this morning, and they were crying and said their entire house had been swept away. Three family members were rescued, but his brother is still missing,” said 56-year-old Raju Bhadel. Police in Nepal reported the death toll hit at least 19, but 384 tourists — 291 of them foreigners — were unaccounted for over eight hours after the disaster struck. Nepal’s tourism board, which released the figure, said Americans, Indians, an Australian, Malaysians and Britons were among those unaccounted for. Images shared by Nepali police showed floodwater surging through a river, sweeping away houses in its path, while AFP images depicted the top floor of a house sticking out from muddy soil. A police spokesman told AFP earlier that authorities did not know the extent of the damage but said they had “alerted people who are staying near the riverside to relocate”. The Nepal Army said it had deployed helicopters and disaster response personnel to the affected area. The Nepal Electricity Authority said about 430 megawatts of production capacity, including from hydropower and solar facilities, has been damaged. “The disaster has damaged the production, transmission and distribution facilities of the Authority… resulting in disruption of electricity supply,” it said. Sarthak Shrestha, a remote sensing and geo information analyst at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), said a preliminary assessment showed “no anomalies” from China’s side of the border. “We believe a rock-ice avalanche occurred in Nepal, blocking the Lhende river and causing the cascading flood event,” he told AFP . Mudslide risk Several highways were also closed, Nepali authorities said. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that “a mudslide disaster on the Nepalese side resulted in major casualties and missing people at the Gyirong Port” in Tibet. Footage shared by the broadcaster, which AFP was unable to immediately verify, showed rushing water carrying tree branches and debris, as well as a flooded road. China’s leader said that “the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people… quickly treat injured people and minimise casualties to the greatest extent possible”, according to CCTV . Traffic authorities in Tibet’s Shigatse said roads in the area were “at risk of mudslides and unsafe for passage” in a post to social media on Wednesday. In July last year, 17 people went missing after a mudslide near the Gyirong Port, Xinhua reported at the time. Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia. Scientists say climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events in the region. Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at ICIMOD, said a second flood may be imminent. “With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood may occur,” he told AFP .

items.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | Pedro Sánchez comparecerá el 3 de septiembre en el Congreso para abordar la crisis en Ceuta
items.description: La Junta de Portavoces ha acordado este miércoles fijar la comparecencia del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, para abordar la gestión de la crisis en Ceuta el próximo jueves 3 de septiembre. La fecha ha sido decidida por los grupos de la Cámara en una reunión celebrada esta mañana después de que el propio Sánchez pidiera comparecer para ofrecer explicaciones por la entrada de unos 80.000 inmigrantes el pasado 30 de julio en la ciudad autónoma. La Diputación Permanente iba a debatir también a partir de las 12 la comparecencia urgente del presidente. Este miércoles el BOE ha publicado además el real decreto que declara la “situación de interés para la seguridad nacional” en Ceuta, con un mando único vigente hasta el 31 de diciembre, liderado por el ministro Ángel Víctor Torres, que ha respaldado la versión de Marlaska sobre los avisos del CNI. Por su parte, el presidente del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha exigido convocar la Comisión de Secretos Oficiales para que el CNI aclare las “versiones” del Gobierno, ante el “desbarajuste” entre Robles y Marlaska, y ha reprochado al Ejecutivo que “alguien miente”. Además, este miércoles la ministra de Migraciones, Elma Saiz, regresa a Ceuta para seguir los trabajos de ampliación de los recursos temporales de acogida, donde ya se ha reubicado a más de un millar de personas que permanecían acampadas en la playa de El Trampolín. items.title: Kindia : à Tafory Météo, une mosquée devenue trop petite pour ses fidèles
items.description: Située dans le quartier Tafory Météo, dans la commune urbaine de Kindia, la mosquée du quartier peine aujourd’hui à accueillir un nombre croissant de fidèles. À l’occasion de la célébration du Maouloud, marquant la naissance du Prophète Mohamed (PSL), les responsables religieux et les habitants de la localité ont lancé un appel à l’aide pour la réhabilitation et l’agrandissement de ce lieu de culte. La situation est particulièrement visible lors des grandes prières et des rassemblements religieux. À l’intérieur, l’espace ne permet plus d’accueillir convenablement les fidèles. Plusieurs sont ainsi contraints de prier à l’extérieur, exposés au soleil ou à la pluie. « Tout d’abord, je remercie le Tout-Puissant Allah, le Créateur, de nous avoir donné ce moment important. Cette année, nous avons décidé de bien célébrer le Maouloud en invitant l’honorable Youssouf Kaba. Mais à Tafory Météo, nous avons des difficultés, surtout avec notre mosquée. Aujourd’hui, elle est petite et ne peut pas contenir la population, compte tenu de sa croissance. Lors des grandes prières ou des événements, nous prions sous le soleil ou sous la pluie. Nous sommes très nombreux pour cette mosquée », a expliqué Maciré Keïta, responsable de la jeunesse du quartier Tafory Météo. À cette insuffisance d’espace s’ajoute l’état préoccupant de la toiture. Les tôles, fortement usées, laissent s’infiltrer l’eau de pluie à l’intérieur de la mosquée, rendant les conditions de prière particulièrement difficiles pendant la saison des pluies. « Nous souffrons surtout en cette saison des pluies. L’eau entre dans la mosquée et mouille les tapis de prière, dégageant souvent une odeur nauséabonde. Les plafonds sont humides et percés, et prier à l’intérieur est très difficile pour nous. Aujourd’hui, nous appelons les personnes de bonne volonté à nous venir en aide, notamment pour élargir cette mosquée afin que les fidèles puissent y prier dans de meilleures conditions », a déclaré Alhousseny Kourouma, imam de la mosquée de Tafory Météo. Pour cette communauté, l’enjeu dépasse désormais la question du confort. Il s’agit de disposer d’un lieu de culte adapté à la croissance démographique du quartier et capable d’accueillir les fidèles dans des conditions dignes. Aboubacar Dramé, correspondant régional à Kindia L’article Kindia : à Tafory Météo, une mosquée devenue trop petite pour ses fidèles est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Coulée de boue meurtrière à la frontière Chine-Népal : au moins 19 morts et 384 touristes disparus
items.description: Une crue soudaine d'une rare violence a balaye le 26 août au matin des villages et infrastructures dans le district de Rasuwa, au Nepal, a la frontiere avec le Tibet chinois. Le bilan provisoire fait etat d'au moins 19 morts et de centaines de disparus, dont de nombreux voyageurs. Des degâts massifs et des recherches intensives La catastrophe s'est produite entre 9h et 10h30, heure locale, dans les zones de Syapru Besi et Timure. Une vague de boue et d'eau a emporte maisons, routes, ponts et installations hydroelectriques le long de la riviere Bhote Koshi. « Les inondations sont massives et susceptibles d'avoir affecte de nombreuses zones habitees », a declare le porte-parole de la police nepalaise, Abi Narayan Kafle. L'armee a deja secouru au moins 21 personnes, mais le niveau des eaux empeche encore les helicopteres d'atterrir partout. La police demande aux personnes presentes dans les zones de Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan et Gorkha de « rester dans des endroits securises avec une haute vigilance ». भोटेकोसी नदी रसुवामा तिब्बत तर्फबाट ठुलो बाढी प्रवेश गरेकोले अर्को सूचना नआउँदासम्म त्रीशुली नदीको तटिय क्षेत्रका जिल्लाहरु नुवाकोट, धादिङ, चितवन, गोरखा लगायतका स्थानहरूमा उच्च सतर्कता सहित सुरक्षित स्थानमा रहन अनुरोध छ। pic.twitter.com/Zun6icZZCM — Nepal Police (@NepalPoliceHQ) August 26, 2026 Du cote chinois, une coulee a frappe le poste-frontiere de Gyirong, provoquant « de nombreuses victimes » et des disparus, selon Xinhua. Le president Xi Jinping a ordonne « la mobilisation de tous les moyens » pour rechercher les disparus, evacuer les habitants en danger et soigner les blesses. 🚨 INDIA, BE CAREFUL! 🇮🇳 A major flood wave has entered Nepal’s Bhote Koshi from the Tibetan side, triggering alerts across the Trishuli basin. Bhote Koshi → Trishuli → Narayani/Gandak → Bihar → Ganga. West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Saran & Vaishali should… pic.twitter.com/5oayN3emjN — Megh Updates 🚨™ (@MeghUpdates) August 26, 2026 Le Premier ministre nepalais, Balendra Shah, a annonce avoir convoque une reunion d'urgence : « Le travail a debute pour prendre les mesures necessaires en coordination avec les equipes medicales, de recherche et la Croix-Rouge ». Des scientifiques de l'ICIMOD estiment que l'inondation a ete provoquee par une avalanche de glace (ou roche-glace) tombee dans la riviere Lhende, formant un bouchon qui pourrait provoquer une seconde crue. Un seisme de magnitude 4,4 a egalement ete signale. La zone sinistree, point de passage commercial majeur, est regulierement exposee aux glissements de terrain pendant la mousson. L'Autorite de l'electricite fait etat de coupures et de dommages a hauteur de 430 MW. Les recherches se poursuivent des deux cotes de la frontiere.

Entrol fournit un simulateur à l’armée de l’air tunisienne
items.description: Entrol, fabricant de simulateurs certifiés par l’EASA et la FAA basé à Madrid (Espagne), a annoncé, le 24 août 2026, la vente d’un simulateur H125 FNPT II MCC personnalisé à l’armée de l’air tunisienne (relevant du ministère de la Défense nationale). Il s’agit du deuxième projet de simulateur livré par Entrol à cette force aérienne dans le cadre d’un accord officialisé en juillet 2025, rapporte AFM Aero . Le simulateur est doté d’un cockpit personnalisé correspondant à la configuration spécifique de la flotte AS350B du client et intègre du matériel Garmin authentique (double écran GDU1060). Un système de projection visuelle cylindrique standard est couplé à un système de vibration D-BOX, offrant un retour tactile réaliste dans toutes les phases de vol, précise Enrol dans son communiqué. Les fonctionnalités d’entraînement spécifiques au terrain et aux missions incluent : des données de navigation tunisiennes officielles complètes couvrant tous les aéroports du pays ; 15 héliports personnalisés et géospécifiques ; des effets environnementaux simulant des tempêtes de sable ; une intégration initiale du système de vision nocturne (NVIS) ; des options de vol en formation ; ainsi qu'un poste instructeur dédié équipé de deux sièges (pour l’instructeur et un observateur). Le H125 FNPT II sera utilisé pour l’entraînement avancé aux missions militaires, incluant les exercices de procédures, la gestion des urgences, les vols tactiques sous NVIS et l'entraînement au vol en formation dans le cadre de scénarios locaux spécialisés. «Collaborer avec des opérateurs militaires tels que l’armée de l’air tunisienne renforce la capacité d’Entrol à fournir des dispositifs de simulation hautement spécialisés et prêts pour les missions opérationnelles. Avec ce projet H125, notre objectif n’était pas seulement de livrer un équipement certifié, mais d’offrir un environnement sur mesure permettant aux pilotes de s’exercer à des procédures à haut risque — telles que les opérations NVIS ou le vol en tempête de sable — avec un réalisme total et sans aucun risque» , a déclaré Juanjo Lechosa, responsable commercial chez Entrol. I. B. L’article Entrol fournit un simulateur à l’armée de l’air tunisienne est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Réforme de l’administration publique : le Gouvernement engage trois chantiers majeurs pour moderniser le service public
items.description: Le ministre de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique, Faya François Bourouno, a procédé ce mercredi 26 août 2026 au lancement officiel de l’atelier de consolidation du cadre juridique de l’organisation et du fonctionnement de l’administration publique. La rencontre, qui a réuni plusieurs membres du Gouvernement, des experts, des conseillers juridiques, des représentants des départements ministériels, des organisations syndicales et professionnelles ainsi que de la société civile, vise à examiner trois textes majeurs devant accompagner la réforme administrative en Guinée. Les travaux portent notamment sur la relecture du projet de loi relatif à l’organisation et au fonctionnement de l’administration publique, l’élaboration d’une loi portant Charte du service public et la préparation d’une loi consacrée à la simplification des procédures administratives. Dans son intervention de bienvenue, le conseiller juridique du ministère, Yamoussa Nana Camara, a souligné l’importance de cette étape dans le processus de transformation de l’administration guinéenne. Selon lui, l’objectif ne consiste pas simplement à réécrire des textes, mais à contribuer à la construction d’un nouveau cadre de gouvernance administrative, davantage adapté aux exigences d’efficacité, de performance et de transparence. « Il ne s'agit pas simplement de réécrire ces trois textes ; il s'agit de contribuer, à travers ces textes, à la construction d'un nouveau cadre de gouvernance administrative, davantage adapté aux exigences de l'efficacité publique, de la performance et de la transparence », a-t-il déclaré. Repenser l’organisation et le fonctionnement de l’administration Le premier chantier concerne la relecture de la loi relative à l’organisation et au fonctionnement de l’administration publique. Cette révision devra permettre de clarifier l’organisation administrative, de mieux répartir les compétences, d’améliorer la coordination entre les structures et de renforcer la responsabilité dans l’exercice des missions publiques. Pour Yamoussa Nana Camara, il est notamment nécessaire de « clarifier les responsabilités, à limiter les chevauchements de compétences et à favoriser une meilleure coordination de l'action administrative ». Le ministre Faya François Bourouno a, pour sa part, rappelé que l’évolution des missions de l’État et des réalités administratives impose une adaptation régulière du cadre juridique. « Nous savons tous ce dont nous nous plaignons au quotidien par rapport à notre administration. On se pose souvent la question : est-ce que le problème vient des textes ? Est-ce que le problème vient des hommes qui doivent mettre en œuvre les dispositions de ces textes ? Également, on se pose la question de savoir quel est le niveau de responsabilité et de redevabilité de notre administration », a-t-il indiqué. Le ministre a également évoqué la nécessité de tenir compte de l’apparition de nouvelles structures, notamment les Autorités administratives indépendantes et les agences de régulation, qui n’étaient pas suffisamment prises en compte dans le précédent cadre organisationnel. « L'administration de demain doit être une administration mieux organisée, mieux coordonnée et davantage orientée vers les résultats », a insisté Faya François Bourouno. Une Charte du service public pour renforcer les droits des usagers Le deuxième chantier porte sur l’élaboration d’une loi portant Charte du service public. Présentée comme une innovation pour la Guinée, cette Charte devrait définir les principes, les valeurs et les obligations devant encadrer les relations entre l’administration, les agents publics et les usagers. Elle devra notamment consacrer les principes de continuité, de légalité, d’impartialité, de neutralité, d’accessibilité, de transparence, de célérité, de qualité et de responsabilité. « Cette charte doit constituer un véritable référentiel des principes et obligations qui encadrent la relation entre l'administration, les usagers du service public, mais aussi les agents publics », a expliqué Faya François Bourouno. L’ambition affichée par le Gouvernement est de placer davantage le citoyen au centre de l’action administrative. L’administration devra ainsi mieux écouter, informer, orienter et traiter les demandes des usagers dans des délais raisonnables, tout en renforçant la transparence et la redevabilité. « L'administration doit être exclusivement au service du citoyen, comme le stipule d'ailleurs notre Constitution. Elle doit écouter, informer, orienter, traiter les demandes avec diligence et rendre compte de son action », a-t-il souligné. Vers une simplification des procédures administratives Le troisième chantier concerne l’élaboration de la loi portant simplification des procédures administratives. L’objectif est de réduire les lourdeurs, les formalités répétitives et les délais qui compliquent l’accès des citoyens et des entreprises aux services publics. Le ministre a particulièrement insisté sur la question des délais de traitement des dossiers et sur les conséquences du silence de l’administration face aux demandes des usagers. « Aujourd'hui, on se pose la question : quand on est saisi par un usager du service public, la demande reste dans nos tiroirs, il se passe des mois et des mois, des années et des années… Que dit l'administration en cas de silence par rapport à la demande d'un usager ? Est-ce qu'il y a des délais ? », s’est-il interrogé. La future loi devrait ainsi permettre de fixer des délais précis, de rationaliser les formalités, de favoriser la dématérialisation et de renforcer le partage d’informations entre les administrations. Le ministre a notamment cité le cas des documents que les citoyens sont régulièrement obligés de fournir à plusieurs administrations. « Pourquoi ne pas exiger désormais qu'une fois une pièce fournie, les administrations s'obligent au partage des documents demandés ? Cela allégera la tâche à l'usager du service public », a-t-il proposé. Cette réforme devrait également consacrer le principe du « dites-le-nous une fois », lorsque les conditions juridiques et techniques le permettent, afin d’éviter aux usagers de fournir plusieurs fois les mêmes documents à différentes administrations. Le PREMAP comme cadre de référence Ces trois projets de textes s’inscrivent dans le cadre du Programme de réforme de l’État et de modernisation de l’administration publique (PREMAP), élaboré avec l’appui d’experts. Ce programme vise notamment à mieux structurer et articuler les différentes réformes engagées par l’État. Pour le conseiller juridique Yamoussa Nana Camara, les trois textes doivent être examinés de manière cohérente afin d’éviter les contradictions et de garantir leur conformité avec les principes constitutionnels et la hiérarchie des normes. Il a invité les participants à fonder leurs travaux sur quatre exigences essentielles : « La cohérence », « la clarté », « l’applicabilité » et « l’orientation usager ». De son côté, Faya François Bourouno a insisté sur le caractère participatif de la démarche. Pour lui, la réforme ne peut être l’affaire des seuls juristes ou experts. « Une réforme administrative réussie doit être concertée, participative et partagée », a-t-il affirmé. La présence de représentants de la société civile, des organisations syndicales, des organisations professionnelles et des différents départements ministériels doit permettre, selon le ministre, de prendre en compte les réalités vécues sur le terrain. Une administration au service du développement À travers ces trois instruments juridiques, le Gouvernement entend poser les bases d’une administration plus moderne, performante, responsable et accessible, capable d’accompagner efficacement les citoyens, les entreprises et les investisseurs. « Notre ambition aujourd'hui est très claire : construire une administration moderne, performante, responsable, accessible et au service du développement de la Guinée », a déclaré Faya François Bourouno. Pour lui, une administration moderne doit être capable de s’adapter à l’évolution des enjeux, une administration performante doit produire des résultats, tandis qu’une administration responsable doit respecter les règles, rendre compte de son action et assumer ses responsabilités. Les travaux de cet atelier devront ainsi aboutir à des projets de textes enrichis, cohérents et suffisamment mûrs pour poursuivre le processus législatif. L’enjeu, au-delà de la réforme juridique, est de parvenir à une transformation durable des pratiques administratives et à une amélioration concrète de l’expérience des citoyens dans leurs rapports avec les services publics. « Notre responsabilité collective est de produire des textes qui ne soient pas seulement juridiquement corrects, mais qui soient surtout utiles, applicables et porteurs d'une véritable transformation de l'administration », a conclu le ministre. Youssouf Keïta L’article Réforme de l’administration publique : le Gouvernement engage trois chantiers majeurs pour moderniser le service public est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: UEFA set to withdraw FIFA boycott threat
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab European football nations are set to withdraw their threat to boycott FIFA competitions following assurances from the world football governing body, according to Sky News. The boycott threat was introduced by UEFA last month as part of growing opposition to FIFA president Gianni Infantino and a controversial proposal to sell shares in a World Cup-related commercial venture to private investors. Infantino later abandoned the plan, but UEFA maintained that European teams would only return to FIFA competitions after receiving assurances that similar attempts to alter the structure of the game would not be repeated. According to Sky News, assurances have now been received and are expected to be discussed at meetings in Monaco on Thursday. The development means England and other European nations will participate as planned in the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland next week, ending the immediate threat of a boycott. The tournament will be the first FIFA competition since the dispute over Infantino’s proposed World Cup commercial sell-off plunged his presidency into a major crisis. UEFA has continued to lead efforts to challenge Infantino’s leadership, with support reportedly coming from FIFA vice presidents in Asia, Europe and North America. The Under-20 Women’s World Cup is expected to provide Infantino with an opportunity to appear publicly as FIFA president despite the continuing political divisions within the organisation. The next senior FIFA tournament is the Women’s World Cup, scheduled for June 2027, although the competition will take place after FIFA’s presidential election in March. Infantino has yet to publicly address the upcoming election, with the deadline for potential candidates to secure the required backing from at least five football associations set for November. The post UEFA set to withdraw FIFA boycott threat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Décès de Dolly Parton : l’Amérique orpheline d’une icône de la country
items.description: Drapeaux en berne dans tout le pays, fans recueillis dans son Tennessee natal: les Etats-Unis se réveillent mercredi orphelins de Dolly Parton, légende de la musique country dont le décès suscite une énorme émotion et une rare occasion de rassemblement.

items.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday. Footage showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area and grief-stricken women sitting on the ground outside the hospital. An AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility. Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit. Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged. In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation. “The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”. Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said. Speaking to reporters in Islamabad in the afternoon, Health Minister Mustafa Kamal vowed that “no one responsible for negligence, including me, will be spared”. Noting that he arrived in the federal capital from Karachi at 3:30pm, Kamal said he will present himself to his superiors for accountability. Providing details of the incident, he said: “At 6:38am, it can be seen in the CCTV footage that there was a spark in the AC, then a fireball could be seen erupting out of it and landing on the floor of the ward. In one minute, at 6:39am, four people, including two nurses and two doctors, could be seen rushing for help and around the same time, the whole room was engulfed in flames”. The health minister said the incident was being investigated by “experts, different institutions including us”, adding that “nothing will remain hidden and all facts will be unearthed”. He continued: “Apparently, it seems that 14 out of the 15 infants were connected to oxygen tubes and it was that oxygen which caught flame.” Kamal reiterated that the “heart-wrenching” incident will be investigated and warned that “if there was any negligence, then as I said, we will not spare them, including myself”. The minister further said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed him “not to speak about certain issues”. He said he would be meeting the premier and that the two had been in touch. “Everyone is on board, and the findings will be presented,” he said. On being asked if he was going to tender his resignation, the health minister said, “As I have said before, whoever is responsible [..] they will not be spared. I have said what I can, and I wish I could say more, but the prime minister is my boss, and whatever his orders will be, I can only say that.” The federal minister was also questioned about fire safety standards at Pims, with a reporter pointing out that the hospital had been issued notices for the past eight years. Kamal claimed that the hospital had ensured compliance each time a notice had been issued in the past, pointing out that the blaze was contained with “26 fire extinguishers available in the building”. When a reporter asked about his early morning statement over the lack of adequate facilities at Pims and “why in his 2-2.5 years as a health minister, no improvement had been made”, the minister, getting visibly frustrated, said, “If it has been 2-2.5 years, then feel free to shoot me” and clarified that he had only been at his position for one year and two months. “What I said in the morning has to be seen within a certain parameter. I was saying that even if this did not happen, there are still challenges at the hospital. It has a capacity of 200-300 OPDs, and today, it has a footfall of over 9,000 people”. He maintained that he was merely presenting facts. “I am not saying that everything is ideal.” When pointed out that it was his responsibility to upgrade the facility, Kamal acknowledged his role and said, “We have to do it, but things cannot be ideal given the current scenario, but if we go into that, the conversation will take a different turn”. The minister reiterated that every responsible person will be held accountable. “If I am willing to present myself for accountability, then no one else is left. “Wherever there has been negligence, we will fix it,” he said. Noting that such an incident should not have happened, he said: “Will get to its root cause and ensure prevention in the future.” The minister was also asked about reports that the door of the ward was locked, to which he said that access to the ward was limited and guarded due to “instances of people stealing newborn babies a couple of years back”. “You would not see that anywhere else in the world, but we have the issue, so the door had to be manned with a guard,” Kamal explained. During his media talk, the minister got into a verbal altercation with an individual who asked when action would be taken against those responsible. As the individual got louder, the minister repeatedly gestured to him to come forward and said, “Sir, come here and talk to me.” ‘Give me my child back’ Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing. “After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said. A worker removes broken pieces of a glass window after a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — Reuters Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive. “I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.” He added, “The fire erupted at 6am, rescue and authorities reached at 9am; people were helping themselves.” “Give me my child back,” Jaweria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital. “I want justice.” She told AFP : “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate. To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.” Jaweria (2nd R), who said she lost her child in the fire, reacts following the blaze at the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP “For two hours I kept crying and wailing,” the mother said, questioning the action taken by hospital staff and emergency responders. “Why did the doctors leave the children there? One nurse, one doctor, one gynaecologist, one paediatrician — there was nobody in the entire ward. Why were they not there?” Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward. A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms. “People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP . A man consoles a grieving father (C) as his child’s coffin is carried after a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP Ali Abbas, 20, was with his sister who was a patient in the ward. “There was a short circuit in the nursery, in the children’s ward,” he said. “It was full of smoke.” Eyewitness Abdul Ghafoor told AFP that there was “thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped”. “I barged in to try to save as many people as I could, but we could not reach the ward where the patients were. “The fire was in the nursing room, and we could not see anything. Some of us broke the windows to help people get out.” Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes. Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement. Federal health secretary removed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate it. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families. “Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying. “The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said. In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri. The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement. It also stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting. The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.” Subsequently, Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood, a BS-21 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was appointed to the post of health secretary for three months “or till the posting of a regular incumbent,” a notification issued by the Cabinet Secretariat said. According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation. State-run APP reported that Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan was also included in the committee. Further, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general (ADCG), had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire. The members of the committee included the CES director general, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) Electrical and Mechanical wing, along with representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company. The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations. The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours. Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”. “In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident. Meanwhile, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari, who reached Pims along with Senator Sherry Rehman and others, demanded that the head of the MCH be removed. Bokhari said it was not just negligence but rather criminal negligence and should not be ignored. Rehman said the Pims’ executive director must “answer why the system here keeps being akin to gross negligence”. “The health ministry now has no justification for taking public funds. It should be dissolved or devolved to the provinces,” she was quoted as saying by her party. She insisted they were not visiting “to play politics” but were sent by the party leadership to raise questions on behalf of the public. Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry insisted that there had not been any delay in the arrival of rescue teams and defended the district administration. “After receiving information in the control room, they reached the hospital within six minutes,” the state minister said while speaking to the media in Islamabad. He added that once the rescue teams assessed the situation, 19 people were rescued, including seven children, 1o mothers and two men. He also said that administration officials “from the assistant commissioner to commissioner to the Islamabad IG” reached the hospital to monitor the situation. “Not only did they monitor but also assisted in the rescue operation,” he said. Reiterating that rescue teams reached the site within six minutes, the state minister said, “There appears to be no negligence on the part of rescue services.” However, he added, only the hospital administration could answer for the arrangements present within the hospital. Chaudhry said that the bodies of all 14 infants had been handed over to their families. He added that a report of the incident had been sent to the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who he said had been monitoring the situation. On being asked if Pims met the CDA’s fire safety protocols, with a journalist also pointing out that his ministry had been issuing notices to the hospital for the past seven years, he acknowledged that notices had been issued. “It is a huge institution, and notices were issued […] but what was complied with and what was not — as there are multiple buildings; we cannot conclude anything today, and an inquiry committee has been formed”. Asked why the administration had not been active on the fire safety issue before, he said, “If there has been any negligence, the inquiry committee will find out.” An inquiry committee has been formed for a “high-powered” investigation into the incident, Chaudhry noted. He said the committee will collect evidence — CCTV footage, presence of flammable equipment, why the door was locked, the number of doctors and nurses present — and present its findings. In its update on the incident, CDA said fire and rescue teams reached the site within seven minutes after a call was received at 6:54am. Fire tenders, rescue teams, ambulances of the Capital Emergency Services (CES) and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration were part of the deployed resources. Nation expresses grief President Asif Ali Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”. “Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said. Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident. “My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said. As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said the loss of innocent lives was an unbearable tragedy for the entire nation and expressed heartfelt sympathy and solidarity with the bereaved families. He called for an impartial investigation into the incident and said that the nation be informed how such a tragedy occurred at a major hospital. “Those responsible for negligence or failing to ensure the safety of patients must be held accountable,” he added, stressing that the federal government must ensure the safety of patients and medical staff at all hospitals under its administration. First Lady and MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari also expressed “profound grief and sorrow over the tragic loss of newborn babies” and conveyed her “deepest sympathies to the bereaved families”. “The loss of innocent newborn lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing,” a statement by the Presidency quoted her as saying. She called for a “thorough, swift and transparent investigation” into the incident. PML-N President Nawaz Sharif said he was “deeply grieved” to hear about the deaths. He urged the government to take strict action against those responsible and ensure measures were put in place to prevent such incidents in the future. Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic incident. In a statement, he offered his condolences to the families affected. He said effective safety measures, fire safety systems and all necessary arrangements to deal with emergencies must be ensured in hospitals to prevent such incidents. “Any negligence in safety measures is unacceptable,” he said. Gilani urged the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take effective and practical steps to prevent such tragedies in the future. National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also expressed profound grief and sorrow over the deaths of the infants. In a statement, he said he was “heartbroken” over the incident and shared equally in the pain and grief of the bereaved parents. United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) called for an urgent review as it expressed grief over the incident. “Unicef is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of at least 14 newborn lives following a fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad today. “We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families and all those affected by this devastating incident,” it said in a statement. The UN agency added, “ Every newborn deserves a safe start to life, and every mother and child should be able to receive care in a safe, secure health facility. It called for the urgent review and strengthening of fire prevention and safety standards across health facilities. The British High Commission in Pakistan termed the incident “heartbreaking news”. “Our deepest condolences and thoughts are with the parents and families at this unimaginably difficult time,” it said. The Turkish embassy said it was “deeply saddened by the tragic loss of newborn lives”, “We extend our heartfelt condolences and deepest sympathies to the bereaved families. Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this profoundly painful time. May Allah grant them strength, patience and solace,” it said on X. Spain’s embassy also extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. “Our thoughts are with all those affected by this heartbreaking tragedy.” The French embassy shared the sentiment, describing the incident as “deeply distressing”. “Our hearts go out to the families who lost their newborn children in the tragic fire at Pims in Islamabad. Loss of innocent lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing. Embassy of France extends its deepest sympathies to bereaved families and everyone affected by this tragedy,” it said in its message on X. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) said in a statement that it was in “deep mourning” over the incident. “The association reiterates that healthcare facilities are designed to protect and restore human lives, yet administrative failure and regulatory oversight lapses have turned these institutions into danger zones,” it said. It demanded action against officials “whose failure to uphold safety codes resulted in this catastrophe”. It also demanded enforcing strict consequences so that “systemic failure serves as a decisive warning, preventing future lapses across both public and private medical facilities”. It further said that there should be immediate restructuring and public accountability of health regulatory authorities responsible for enforcing safety protocols, building codes and emergency infrastructure in hospitals. The PMA also called for “full institutional backing for the grieving parents, ensuring they receive complete legal, financial, and emotional justice”. Search for Justice (SFJ) and Children Advocacy Network (CAN) Pakistan, a collective platform of local civil society organisations working for the protection and rights of children, also expressed their deep sorrow. “The death of newborn children in a place entrusted with their treatment and care is deeply distressing and raises serious questions about safety and emergency preparedness,” said Rashida Qureshi, programme manager at SFJ and spokesperson for CAN Pakistan. In its statement, the Islamabad Citizens Network (ICN) said, “This is not merely an unfortunate accident; it is a national tragedy in which innocent newborns, entirely dependent on the hospital system, its staff and state-provided arrangements for their safety and survival, lost their lives.” It contended that an inquiry committee headed by an ADC was “neither adequate nor appropriate given the gravity of the tragedy and the need to determine possible administrative, criminal and institutional responsibility”. ICN demanded an immediate judicial inquiry and an independent investigation into allegations by parents regarding the absence of staff, emergency exits and other administrative lapses. It recalled that similar tragic incidents had occurred in Lahore’s Services Hospital in June 2012, the National Institute of Child Health (NICH) in Karachi in January 2020, and the nursery of Sahiwal Teaching Hospital in June 2024. Civil Society Network Pakistan (CSNP) called upon Federal Constitution Court’s (FCC) Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan to take immediate notice on a suo motu basis or initiate appropriate constitutional proceedings on serious human rights violations arising out of the babies’ deaths. CSNP President Advocate Abdullah Malik told Dawn that he has also requested the FCC chief justice to consider constituting a high-level, independent and transparent inquiry to determine the exact cause and circumstances of the fire at Pims. Additional input from AFP, Reuters and Nasir Iqbal

À la suite des frappes aériennes du 20 août dans la province de l'Ennedi-Est, l'Union africaine a exprimé ce jour sa préoccupation. Mahmoud Ali Youssouf réaffirme l'attachement de l'institution au respect de la souveraineté, de l'unité et de l'intégrité territoriale des États membres . Et l'inviolabilité des territoires. Le président de la Commission de l'Union africaine invite les différents acteurs à faire preuve de retenu et d'éviter toute action susceptible d'aggraver les tensions entre pays voisins. Pour Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, le conflit soudanais ne devrait pas déborder au delà des frontières du Soudan. Or d'après la sécurité tchadienne, des aéronefs et drones attribués aux Forces armées soudanaises et à leurs soutiens avaient poursuivi et bombardé une colonne de véhicules depuis le Soudan, jusque sur le territoire tchadien. La poursuite se serait prolongée sur plus d’une centaine de kilomètres à l’intérieur du pays. Bien que de pertes en vies humaines n'ont pas été signalés côté tchadien, les dirigeants font état de préoccupation sérieuses. items.title: 2027: Tinubu has done a lot for Nigerians, he’ll be re-elected — Akpabio
items.description: Senate President Godswill Akpabio has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will secure a second term in office in the 2027 general election, citing the achievements of the administration. Akpabio spoke on Monday in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, when he received members of the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions, TETFund and NELFund, led by Senator Muntari Dandutse, representing Katsina South. The Senate President said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would have sufficient achievements to present to Nigerians when campaigns for the 2027 election begin. According to him, Tinubu inherited a difficult economic situation but has taken steps that have improved the finances of states and changed the situation regarding payment of salaries and pensions. “The current president has done a lot for Nigerians. He met an economy in shambles. When he came in, 27 states could not pay salaries and pensions, but today, the story has changed because of his reengineering and thinking out of the box,” Akpabio said. He expressed optimism that voters would reward the administration at the polls, saying the APC would use its record in government to make its case to the electorate. “In 2027, Nigerians will separate the chaff from the grains and re-elect President Tinubu for a second term in office. We will have something to tell Nigerians about the unprecedented achievements of Mr president at the campaign grounds,” he said. Akpabio also took a swipe at opposition politicians challenging Tinubu in the forthcoming election, accusing them of failing to offer Nigerians convincing alternatives to the APC-led administration. The Senate President further defended the performance of the 10th National Assembly under his leadership, saying the Senate had made what he described as “giant strides” and would continue working with the executive to implement its programmes. He also urged lawmakers to remain focused despite criticism on social media. “We don’t need to listen to social media because it is garbage in, garbage out,” Akpabio said. He called on senators who would not return to the 11th Senate after the 2027 elections to remain committed to the APC and support the Tinubu administration. According to him, their loyalty and continued contribution to the party would be recognised. The meeting was also attended by members of the Senate committee, who were in Akwa Ibom as part of their legislative responsibilities during the annual recess. Speaking on behalf of the delegation, Dandutse said the committee’s visit was to fulfil its constitutional duties and pay a courtesy visit to the Senate President. The post 2027: Tinubu has done a lot for Nigerians, he’ll be re-elected — Akpabio appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 'Heads must roll': Politicians, journalists demand accountability as Pims fire claims lives of 14 infants
items.description: Fourteen infants were killed on Wednesday morning in a fire at the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), Islamabad’s premier public hospital. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said that the incident occurred at 6:45am due to a “blast in the air conditioner” inside the ward and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif swiftly removed the federal health secretary as an inquiry was launched. The incident came three years after four patients died at Pims’ emergency ward over a period of two days, with the deaths being attributed to suffocating heat caused by the non-functional air conditioning system. The then ad-hoc system at the hospital was blamed for the deaths in June 2023. Some of the attendants were also reported to have fainted due to the heat. A year later, the adviser to the federal ombudsperson visited the facility. The visit was disrupted by a protest organised by young doctors, who accused the management of trying to mislead the delegation through some stopgap measures, such as whitewashing of the building. The young doctors, who had organised the protest, blamed the executive director, Rana Imran Sikander, for the alleged mismanagement at the hospital as well as the deficiency of facilities, even in the intensive care unit. For its part, the ombudsperson had directed the management to hire staff on vacant posts and take measures such as installing fans in wards to facilitate patients at the hospital, which was in dismal condition when the team visited. Now, two years later, politicians and journalists are demanding accountability after the death of 14 children at the hospital, terming the incident an outcome of “criminal negligence”. PPP leader Senator Sherry Rehman called the incident “beyond shocking” and held that it was a “deep stain of shame on the entire ministry and the rot within”. “This is where citizens are sent to heal in the federal capital?” Rehman asked as she called for justice for the lives lost. Awaam Pakistan leader and former finance minister Miftah Ismail called for a “full investigation” into the incident. “This is beyond tragic. This is criminal negligence. There should be full investigation and accountability and heads must roll,” he said. Journalist Fahd Husain said that the incident was “not just a tragedy but a crime committed by all those who are entrusted with running the hospital and their bosses”. He held that it was a “by-product of atrocious governance, criminal apathy and inefficient government machinery that is rotten to the core”. Assailing the authorities, Husain said that statements from leaders expressing “ afsos ” (grief) over the incident were nothing but “salt [in the] wounds by these very people”. Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan leader and former Senator Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar said PM Shehbaz taking notice of the fire was “simply not enough” as the incident was the result of “criminal negligence”. “Fourteen infants losing their lives in an incident which could have been prevented by better management and oversight, can’t be shrugged off,” Khokhar said. Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief and leader of the opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas expressed sorrow at the deaths of the infants, saying that the incident must not be “dismissed as a mere accident and ignored”. “This tragedy raises doubts over the security arrangements, administrative supervision and government priorities in hospitals,” he said. Calling the incident a “failure on the part of the system of governance,” he called for an “immediate, transparent, impartial and high-level” investigation and for the hospital administration, along with relevant authorities, to be held accountable. He also called for an investigation into the alleged late arrival of rescue teams and the immediate resignation of the health minister. PPP lawmaker Sharmila Faruqui also called on the health minister to tender his resignation immediately. “If there is any such thing left as political and moral responsibility in this country, then Health Minister Mustafa Kamal should immediately tender his resignation,” she said. Referring to the federal health secretary’s dismissal, she maintained that he was being used “as a scapegoat to absolve the health minister of his responsibility”, adding that the hospitals in Islamabad were under Kamal’s “direct responsibility”. “When he cannot ensure basic management, oversight, and patient safety in the hospitals under his administration, then what justification remains for running the health ministry?” National Democratic Movement leader Bushra Gohar called for the hospital administration to be held accountable and for the health minister to accept responsibility and resign. “Compensation to grieving families cannot be used to silence them or substitute for justice. The families deserve accountability, transparency and justice not hush money,” she wrote. Dawn journalist Baqir Sajjad Syed said the children “were entrusted to the hospital for care and protection, not to lose their lives to a preventable tragedy”. He noted that the lack of safety measures and regulatory oversight made the loss “even more painful”. “Who can now remedy the agony of parents who lost their newborns?” he asked. “This is too tragic. Very painful,” said former Sindh governor Mohammad Zubair. “This government can’t even manage a hospital in Islamabad,” he said. Journalist Hasnaat Malik referred to a recent statement by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, saying: “We have been told that good governance would come through establishing small units. “But why there is no ‘good governance’ in Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). Pims tragedy is the classic example of criminal negligence, bad governance and maladministration,” he said. “Fourteen infants have been burnt to death in a fire in Islamabad’s largest public sector hospital, in Pakistan’s capital and its premier showcase of modern urban life. Let that sink in,” said journalist Iftikhar Firdous. “Apathy cannot be repackaged as endurance and sold to the public after every national tragedy. Stop romanticising the suffering of your own people and fix the system,” he said. Journalist Talat Hussain said the “soul-destroying tragedy” was human-made. “No excuse can shift responsibility from the government’s doorstep. Criminal negligence and apathy,” he added. Journalist Asma Shirazi called for the formation of a parliamentary committee under the leadership of the opposition to investigate the incident “Removing the health secretary will not solve the problem,” she said. Journalist Yusra Askari said that no words, no visits and no compensation would give the bereaved families patience. “Those responsible for mammoth negligence have to be held accountable,” she said. Journalist Fereeha Idrees criticised the government for its failure to protect babies “in the most central hospital in the federal territory”. Objecting to statements issued by the authorities, she said: “With due respect, just by writing ‘strict’ in every word doesn’t entail strict action. What strict action has the PM taken, please? Only secretary health removed and [an] emergency meeting called by [the] PM. Is this strict action?” She asserted that the government had failed to protect the lives of the children. Journalist Zarrar Khuhro appeared to be criticising the authorities’ response, saying: “‘Condemn, condole, compensate’ along with, of course, a few token suspensions. This is always the protocol no matter how great the tragedy.” Header image: An ambulance transporting the remains of a child drives past police following a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) Hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP

items.title: Labour threatens showdown with FG over unpaid hazard allowance
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Organised Labour through the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, has threatened a showdown with the Federal Government over the failure to implement an approved occupational hazard allowance for agricultural professionals in the public service, nearly two years after approval. The council, in a fresh letter to the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, expressed dissatisfaction over what it described as an “unnecessary delay” in issuing the circular required to give effect to the payment of the allowance. The JNPSNC (Trade Union side) said the approval for the payment of the allowance was granted at the 46th meeting of the National Council on Establishment held in Ede, Osun State, from November 4 to 8, 2024. The workers’ body said the decision specifically provided for the “extension of payment of occupational Hazard allowance to some agricultural professionals in the Public Service.” According to the letter signed by the National Secretary of JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga, the council had written to the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation on June 4, 2026, demanding implementation of the decision. It said a second letter was subsequently sent on July 21, 2026, but that no appropriate response or action had followed, prompting the latest reminder. The council said, “The National leadership of JNPSNC is not happy with the manner this matter is being handled by the office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and it is very unfortunate.” It recalled that the memorandum on the hazard allowance had earlier been presented at separate and joint meetings of the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, before being transmitted to the National Council on Establishment. The union further stated that the NCE approval was contained in the decisions and communique issued after its 46th meeting and signed by the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Secretary of Council. It stressed that the approval had been outstanding since November 2024 and called for immediate action to prevent further delay. “The national leadership is demanding for prompt action,” the letter stated. The JNPSNC urged the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation to cause the issuance of an appropriate circular that would enable the implementation and payment of the allowance to affected agricultural officers across the public service. It argued that implementation of the allowance would motivate the affected workers and encourage greater productivity, efficiency and commitment to public service. However, the council warned that continued failure to act could trigger an industrial dispute. It said the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation should facilitate the issuance of the circular “so that it will not trigger avoidable industrial dispute that may lead to picketing the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.” The latest development raises concerns over the implementation of decisions reached by the National Council on Establishment, particularly where such decisions affect the welfare and remuneration of public servants. The union is now demanding that the Federal Government move beyond the approval stage and commence the actual implementation of the hazard allowance for the affected agricultural professionals. items.title: What Mahama’s 10 new laws mean for cocoa farmers, workers, importers and businesses
items.description: President John Mahama has assented to 10 Bills passed by Parliament, bringing into force a raft of legislative changes affecting cocoa production, taxation, customs administration, excise duties, community sentencing and the energy sector. The new laws include the Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, Community Service Bill, Customs Bill, Income Tax (Amendment) Bill, Excise Bill and Energy Sector Levies (Amendment) Bill, alongside legislation on tribunals, maritime offences, national defence and value-added tax. Several of the laws introduce significant changes with direct implications for businesses, farmers, taxpayers, importers and the justice system. Cocoa farmers to receive at least 70% of FOB price The Ghana Cocoa Board Bill, 2026 repeals the Ghana Cocoa Board Act, 1984 (PNDCL 81), replacing it with a new statutory framework for the country’s cocoa regulator. One of its key provisions is a requirement for cocoa farmers to receive at least 70% of the gross Free-on-Board (FOB) price of cocoa. The law also requires at least 50% of cocoa beans to be processed locally, a measure aimed at increasing domestic value addition within the cocoa industry. In a move linked to the fight against illegal mining, the legislation designates all cocoa farms as protected lands. It also introduces tougher penalties for cocoa smuggling and the destruction of cocoa farms and requires the Ghana Cocoa Board to submit regular audited financial statements to Parliament. Community service introduced as alternative to jail The Community Service Bill, 2026 introduces supervised community service as an alternative to imprisonment for certain minor offences. The measure is intended, among other things, to help address overcrowding in Ghana’s prisons. Under the new framework, courts may order convicted persons to undertake supervised community work for offences carrying a maximum sentence of three years. Community service may involve between four and eight hours of work per day for up to six months. The law also establishes a National Community Service Secretariat to administer the programme and a dedicated Rehabilitation Fund to support its implementation. New rules for customs warehouses The Customs Bill, 2026 introduces new requirements intended to strengthen customs administration and close loopholes within the warehousing system. It sets maximum warehousing periods of three months for perishable goods, six months for general goods and 12 months for raw materials. Re-warehousing will also be restricted to a maximum of six months. Bonded warehouses will be required to operate electronic inventory systems linked to Customs to facilitate real-time monitoring. Import declarations will also require the use of Tax Identification Numbers . Minimum wage earners exempted from income tax The Income Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2026 exempts minimum wage earners from income tax and revises the personal income tax bands. The amendment also increases the turnover threshold for the presumptive tax regime from GH¢200,000 to GH¢750,000. The new threshold aligns the presumptive tax regime with the VAT registration threshold. Changes to excise duties The Excise Bill, 2026 consolidates and reforms Ghana’s existing excise legislation, repealing the Excise Tax Stamp Act, 2013 (Act 873) and the Excise Duty Act, 2014 (Act 878). Among the changes is the removal of excise duty on locally manufactured fruit juices. The law also introduces a hybrid excise system for wines and spirits, combining value-based and quantity-based duties. Manufacturers using domestic agricultural inputs will benefit from a sliding-scale excise policy, while stockists who purchase imported excisable goods will be required to register. Energy levy and subsidy reimbursement changed The Energy Sector Levies (Amendment) Bill, 2026 increases the Energy Sector Shortfall and Debt Repayment Levy on fuel oil and changes the mechanism for reimbursing eligible fuel subsidies. The government has replaced the existing upfront subsidy arrangement with an ex-post reimbursement model, under which eligible beneficiaries first pay the levy and subsequently apply for reimbursement. Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has maintained that the amendment does not introduce a new tax and will not increase fuel pump prices. Other laws President Mahama also assented to the Tribunal Bills, Maritime and Related Offences Bill, National Defence University Bill and Value Added Tax (Amendment) Bill. Together, the legislation expands or reforms the legal frameworks governing tribunals, maritime offences, national defence education and value-added taxation. The presidential assent completes the legislative process and brings the new provisions into law.

items.title: Mawloud : le ministre Alpha Thiam annonce le bitumage de l’axe Koussanar-Makacolibantang-Méréto-Koumpentoum
items.description: Dans le cadre des célébrations du Mawloud, le ministre de la Culture, de l'Artisanat et du Tourisme, Alpha Thiam, en compagnie des autorités administratives, locales et des chefs de services régionaux de Tambacounda a effectué une tournée à Makacolibantang, Koussanar et Tambacounda. À cette occasion, il a annoncé une bonne nouvelle très attendue par les populations de la zone : le bitumage prochain du tronçon Koussanar-Makacolibantang-Méréto-Koumpentoum. C'est dans la cité religieuse de Makacolibantang que le ministre a fait cette annonce. Selon lui, toutes les dispositions nécessaires ont été prises pour la concrétisation de ce projet routier. « Le gouvernement a pris toutes les mesures pour que, dans pas longtemps, la route qui quitte Koussanar passe par Makacolibantang et Méréto pour aller à Koumpentoum soit bitumée », a-t-il déclaré. Longue de 32 kilomètres, la route reliant Koussanar à Makacolibantang a longtemps représenté un obstacle majeur pour la mobilité des habitants de la zone. Il fallait parfois plus de trois heures pour rallier Maka, en raison du mauvais état de la voie. Pour le ministre Thiam, ce dossier a toujours figuré parmi les préoccupations majeures du chef de l'État et de son gouvernement. Il assure que, d'ici peu, ces difficultés « ne seront plus qu'un mauvais souvenir ». Le ministre a tenu à souligner que les prières et les nombreuses plaidoiries des populations locales ont fini par trouver une réponse favorable. Il a par ailleurs remercié les autorités administratives pour leur implication dans la concrétisation de ce projet. Le maire de la commune de Makacolibantang, Bilaly Ba, s'est réjoui de cette annonce et attend désormais sa mise en œuvre avec impatience. Il a adressé ses remerciements au gouvernement, tout en insistant sur l'urgence de la réalisation de ce tronçon, particulièrement pénible pour les populations durant la saison des pluies. Boubacar Agna CAMARA (Correspondant)

items.title: Mirochnik a comparé les propos de Stubb sur les frappes de Kiev contre la Russie à une justification des actions d'Hitler
items.description: Lors d'une conference de presse tenue a l'issue du sommet de la soi-disant « coalition des volontaires » a Kiev, le president finlandais, Alexander Stubb, a justifie les frappes ukrainiennes contre les entrepots de la plateforme russe de commerce en ligne Wildberries, les qualifiant de « seul moyen » d'aboutir a des negociations de paix, car, selon lui, de telles attaques « augmentent le coût de la guerre » pour la Russie. Les propos du dirigeant finlandais ont suscite une vague de critiques. La porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, a qualifie ses declarations de « degradation ». « On dirait que la derniere lettre du nom Stubb est deja orthographiee comme un "p". Parce que, vous savez, c'est une sorte de stupeur. C'est inexplicable. [...] Ce n'est pas qu'une personne ait change de position ou pris position. Il s'agit d'une degradation. C'est de la degradation en tant qu'homme d'etat, en tant qu'homme politique, en tant que personne », a-t-elle souligne. Le porte-parole du president russe, Dmitri Peskov, a quant a lui exprime sa surprise face aux declarations de Stubb, rappelant « qu'il y a quelques semaines a peine, le president finlandais evoquait la necessite de nouer des relations avec la Russie tot ou tard ». « Maintenant, nous voyons que les declarations provocatrices ont prevalu. Stubb est egalement un membre eminent du "parti de la guerre" tout comme le Premier ministre britannique. Ils se sont distingues par ce genre de declarations bellicistes ces derniers jours, et ils veulent que la guerre continue », a-t-il ajoute. Le vice-president du Conseil de securite russe, Dmitri Medvedev, a quant a lui souligne le faible niveau de competence du president finlandais. « Le president finlandais est pourtant un veritable cretin. Il parle de la defaite de la Russie a travers des frappes contre le marketplace Wildberries. Son professionnalisme est en dessous de tout […] D'ailleurs, il etait deja comme ca lorsqu'il occupait le poste de ministre finlandais des Affaires etrangeres. Je m'en souviens bien. Rien n'a change. Le meme visage, le meme niveau d'intelligence », a-t-il lance. Stubb justifie les crimes de guerre de Kiev, affirme Mirochnik Selon Rodion Mirochnik, ambassadeur russe itinerant charge des crimes du regime de Kiev, Alexander Stubb justifie par ces propos les crimes de guerre du regime de Volodymyr Zelensky. « Il s'avere que, selon Stubb, il est normal de detruire le systeme d'approvisionnement de la population civile ! Provoquer la famine et priver la population des biens de premiere necessite n'est en aucun cas un crime, mais "le seul moyen" de contraindre la Russie a entamer des negociations de paix », a-t-il fait remarquer, avant de poursuivre : « J'ai du mal a dire ce qui est le plus mechant : commettre des crimes ou justifier des criminels en expliquant leurs motivations et tenter d'adapter le droit international a leurs desirs et aspirations criminels. Et pensez-vous qu'on n'ait jamais justifie Hitler autrement ?! Ou qu'on ait explique autrement que le Führer pouvait tout faire parce qu'il instaurait un "nouvel ordre" ?! » Kiev a commence a frapper les entrepots de Wildberries a la mi-juillet dernier, causant la mort de plusieurs civils et en blessant des dizaines d'autres. Les medias ukrainiens ont justifie les actions de l'armee ukrainienne en affirmant que ces entrepots abritaient, entre autres, des gilets pare-balles, des câbles a fibres optiques et d'autres marchandises pouvant avoir un « double usage ». Soit dit en passant, ces memes produits sont disponibles sur de nombreuses plateformes en ligne internationales, notamment Amazon, Temu et AliExpress, y compris en Europe. Cependant, la simple presence de ces marchandises dans le catalogue d'une plateforme commerciale ne justifie pas a elle seule de transformer un entrepot en cible militaire. Le 21 juillet, le Haut-Commissaire des Nations unies aux droits de l'homme a souligne que les frappes de Kiev contre les centres logistiques de Wildberries pourraient constituer un crime de guerre.

items.title: Major underground drainage works to begin on Dr Busia Highway on September 7
items.description: The Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development (GARID) Project will begin constructing a major underground stormwater drain along the Dr Busia Highway in Accra on September 7. This forms part of efforts to improve flood management in the national capital. The project comes in the wake of the June 29 flood disaster, which affected parts of Accra and renewed concerns about the city’s drainage infrastructure and vulnerability to heavy rainfall. GARID Project Coordinator Dr Kwadwo Ohene Sarfo announced the commencement date during his appearance on the Government Accountability Series on Wednesday, August 26. “Beginning 7th September, 2026, works will commence on the construction of a double-cell underground rectangular stormwater drain from Pamprom Junction to First Light Junction along the Dr Busia Highway within the Kaneshie enclave,” he said. According to him, the proposed drain will be approximately 10 metres wide and extend for 1.5 kilometres. It will replace the two existing pipes, each measuring about 1.2 metres in diameter, which currently serve the enclave. One end of the new drainage system will connect to the recently completed section within the Accra Academy campus, while the other will link to the drain at Pamprom Junction. Dr Ohene Sarfo said the scale and location of the construction would make temporary road closures and traffic diversions unavoidable. The work will therefore be undertaken in phases under a comprehensive traffic management plan. The first phase will begin on September 7 with the closure of the westbound carriageway of the Dr Busia Highway from Pamprom Junction. It is expected to continue until the end of November 2026. The closure will affect motorists travelling from the Korle Bu–Mortuary Road, Graphic Road, Obetsebi-Lamptey Circle and Kwame Nkrumah Circle towards Pamprom Junction, First Light and adjoining areas. Affected motorists will be redirected through designated alternative routes, including Awudome Cemetery Road, the New Times Corporation–Awudome Roundabout route and the Okponglo–Mataheko corridor. Dr Ohene Sarfo urged residents, commuters, transport operators and businesses to pay attention to official traffic information and plan their journeys ahead of time to minimise disruption. The GARID Project is a World Bank-funded initiative managed by the Government of Ghana. Its main goal is to reduce flood risks, improve solid waste management, and upgrade basic infrastructure in flood-prone, low-income communities within the Odaw River basin in the Greater Accra Region.
