items.title: The Nigerian Fan’s Roadmap to World Cup Betting: Decoding Top Tips, Odds, and Match Previews
items.description: If you’ve ever stepped foot in Lagos, Abuja, or Enugu during a major tournament, you’ll know that football isn’t just a pastime in Nigeria; it’s a shared language. The air carries a unique energy, a mix of optimism and chatter that you can hear from several streets away. When the World Cup comes around, this passion reaches a completely different level. Every corner shop, barber’s salon, and local roadside joint transforms into a makeshift studio where amateur pundits debate tactics with the intensity of professional managers. How many times have you found yourself in a heated debate over a starting lineup before a ball has even been kicked? It’s all part of the charm. Nigeria’s Football Passion: How Local Communities and Vanguardngr’s Sports Columns Drive Fan Engagement During Global Championships For decades, the foundations of these passionate debates have been laid by the country’s sports journalists. If you want to know what makes the local football community tick, you only need to look at the sports pages of Vanguard newspapers, widely known online as Vanguardngr. Long before smartphones became part of everyday life, fans would queue up at newsstands early in the morning just to read the latest columns, sharing a single copy amongst friends until the pages were worn thin. The beauty of these columns lies in how they connect with the everyday supporter. They don’t just report the score; they capture the emotion, the local rivalries, and the cultural context of the game. During global championships, these sports pages act as a bridge between the street debates and the high-tech stadiums where the matches are played. They give fans the vocabulary to explain why a midfield partnership isn’t working or why a particular manager’s defensive strategy is doomed to fail. This shared knowledge builds a sense of community, ensuring that whether you’re watching the match in a crowded viewing centre or on a quiet television at home, you’re part of a massive, collective experience. You’ll often see grandparents, who still remember the legendary teams of the 1980s, sitting alongside younger fans who are obsessed with European league statistics. They might disagree on which era had the better players, but they’re completely united in their love for the game. This intergenerational dialogue is kept alive by the timeless analysis found in local sports journalism, proving that while players and tactics may change, the underlying passion remains exactly the same. The Evolution of Digital Sports Media in West Africa: Real-Time Match Summaries, Live Updates, and Mobile fan Culture While the print edition of Vanguard still holds a special place in the hearts of many, the way West African fans interact with football has undergone a massive shift over the last decade. It’s hard to overstate how much mobile technology has reshaped the fan experience across the region. Today, the conversation has largely moved from physical newsstands to digital forums, WhatsApp groups, and real-time social media platforms. Imagine being caught in the notorious Lagos traffic while a crucial group-stage match is underway. A few years ago, you’d have been relying on patchy radio commentary or waiting until you got home to hear the result. Now, you can follow every pass, tackle, and VAR decision through real-time match summaries and live updates on your phone. Who hasn’t spent half a match refreshing their screen, praying that their mobile connection doesn’t drop at the worst possible moment? Mobile data has become the lifeblood of West African fan culture, allowing supporters to stay connected to the action regardless of where they are. This digital evolution has also given rise to a highly interactive mobile fan culture. It’s no longer just about passively watching a game; it’s about participating in it. items.title: The German Far Right Is Poised for a Breakthrough
items.description: I magine that it’s October 2026, and one of Germany’s 16 federal states has come under the control of a far-right government for the first time since the Nazi era. With an absolute majority in the state Parliament and one of its own installed as state premier, the Alternative for Germany, or AfD, quickly begins implementing its agenda. The interior minister announces an emergency remigration program: abolishing asylum, revoking the residence permit of any foreigner convicted of a crime, pledging to review all naturalization decisions made during this century, and incarcerating those designated for deportation. The government stops classifying Ukrainians as war refugees and ends their social benefits. European Union flags disappear from public buildings. The mainstream press is shunned in favor of influencers aligned with the party’s ideology. The government authorizes vigilante groups to act as an auxiliary police force in regions with high crime rates. This hasn’t happened, but it’s not merely hypothetical either. The AfD is projected to win an election next month in Saxony-Anhalt, a central German state of some 2 million people. An anti-racism NGO in Berlin, the Amadeu Antonio Foundation, created this scenario based on the far-right party’s own election manifesto and the statements of its representatives. For decades, right-wing politics have carried particular weight in Germany, where atonement for the Holocaust includes mandatory education about the rise of National Socialism. The far right was long relegated to the fringes, its most ardent members easily identified as skinheads decked out in leather. But the AfD, founded in 2013 as a mild euroskeptic party led mostly by conservative economists opposed to eurozone bailouts, is now Germany’s most important right-wing force since the Nazis. At the national level, the AfD is the most popular party, supported by more than a quarter of voters in recent polls. It leads both of the traditional broad-based parties, the center-right Christian Democrats and the center-left Social Democrats. Its base of support is in the formerly Communist east—generally poorer, older, and angrier than the rest of Germany. And that’s where it’s poised for a breakthrough later this summer. In past state elections, other parties have contorted themselves to keep the far-right faction out of governing coalitions, maintaining a so-called firewall even when the AfD has won the most votes. That may not be possible in Saxony-Anhalt, where ahead of a September 6 vote, the AfD is polling at more than 40 percent. If smaller parties fail to reach the required 5 percent threshold to enter Parliament, this kind of showing by the AfD could be enough for it to win an outright majority, meaning that it wouldn’t need cooperation from other parties to govern. Suddenly, Saxony-Anhalt would become a testing ground for AfD policies. If the AfD doesn’t reach that threshold, the spotlight would turn to the Christian Democratic Union, the party of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The Christian Democrats would face a dilemma: whether to breach the firewall and work with the AfD or join hands with the far-left party Die Linke in a last-ditch effort to keep the far right from taking power. In fact, the Christian Democrats have a policy, formalized in 2018 and known as an incompatibility resolution, against working with either party. Andreas Rödder, a historian who previously headed the center-right party’s fundamental-values commission, told me that the decision didn’t generate much controversy within the party at the time because the matter was mostly symbolic; the center-right party, then dominated by Chancellor Angela Merkel, had other choices for governing partners. At that time, German politics remained fairly stable, relatively speaking, as anti-establishment forces shook up other Western democracies. For many in Germany, this was a point of pride, a sign that the country had learned from its history, that it knew where political fanaticism led. Less than a decade later, Germany no longer appears immune to extremism, and the stable politics that once attested to its moral redemption are “on the brink of being fundamentally shattered,” Rödder said. The country’s domestic intelligence agency has classified Saxony-Anhalt’s branch of the AfD as a right-wing extremist group. Some voters support the party because of that hard-right agenda. Others are drawn to it for contrarian reasons: to register their dissent against elite gatekeepers, whether in the security service, the judiciary, or the media. In this way, their vote is a version of the declaration once made by the Russian literary critic Vissarion Belinsky: “Negation is my god.” “Every organ of elite opinion tells people they can’t vote for the AfD,” a German diplomat told me. “And many people respond by saying, ‘Hell yes, we can.’” W hy does an election in a relatively small German state matter? Because what happens in Germany matters. That’s been the nature of the German problem for almost two centuries—what to do with this country, larger and more prosperous than its neighbors, that has caused so much torment for Europe and for the world. The problem arose with the Franco-Prussian War and the unification of Germany in 1871. It returned in monstrous form during both world wars. And it recurred with German reunification in 1990. The German question is back as the country breaks with postwar taboos. Germany is rearming, spending billions to turn its army into the strongest in Europe. Its steadfast support for Israel has been shaken by the extremism of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government. And in Saxony-Anhalt as well as other German regions, even if not yet nationally, the far right appears on the cusp of claiming power. [ From the January issue: The new German war machine ] Germany’s situation isn’t unique; what’s striking in a country where historians have debated whether a Sonderweg , or “special path,” produced destructive nationalism is how much it mirrors what’s happening elsewhere in Europe. Marine Le Pen, the far-right French firebrand, is leading in polls ahead of a presidential election next year. Nigel Farage’s Reform UK remains in a strong position in Britain. Giorgia Meloni already leads a far-right government in Italy, representing a party that traces its roots to the country’s postwar neofascist movement. Saxony-Anhalt is following these same trends. But the circumstances command greater attention. As Henry Morgenthau Jr., President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s treasury secretary, titled his postwar book on the defeated Axis power, Germany Is Our Problem . Saxony-Anhalt is sometimes called the heartland of German history. It’s the birthplace of the Protestant Reformation, where Martin Luther nailed his 95 theses to the church door in Wittenberg. Cities such as the capital, Magdeburg, were important centers of the Holy Roman Empire. In the 20th century, modernism flourished in the region, which has Germany’s highest concentration of Bauhaus architecture. It’s long been a hub of the chemical and coal-mining industries. During the Cold War, the territory fell on the eastern side of the Iron Curtain, and the state still faces structural problems left over from post-reunification deindustrialization and out-migration, including higher rates of poverty and unemployment than the national average. The psychic effect also lingers. Until 1990, there was no genuine democracy; freedom and civil rights were curtailed. “In some quarters,” Detlef Gürth, a member of the ruling Christian Democrats in Saxony-Anhalt’s state Parliament, told me, there is still a “pronounced desire for a ‘strongman,’ a messiah who dictates the course of action and takes care of everything.” Two recent events crystallize the state’s misfortune and the feeling among many residents that things aren’t working. In December 2024, a Saudi-born doctor drove a rented SUV through a crowded Christmas market in Magdeburg, killing six people and injuring hundreds more. Authorities said the perpetrator was an anti-Islam activist sympathetic to far-right groups, but terrorist violence of any kind, the facts notwithstanding, played into the far right’s hands. The following year, the California-based Intel Corporation canceled plans for a €30 billion chip factory in Magdeburg, which would have been the biggest-ever foreign direct investment in Germany. The episodes were unrelated; the company said it had simply grown too fast, although a government minister also found an explanation in “Donald Trump’s ‘America First’ philosophy.” Together, however, they contributed to a gathering feeling of precarity and bad luck. The AfD promises to shake up the system. Its 35-year-old front man, Ulrich Siegmund, is a perpetually smiling social-media sensation. He is a salesman by trade, the founder of a fragrance company called Berlin-Duftet, whose name means literally “Berlin smells good.” Der Spiegel , the prestigious German news magazine, recently branded him “the most dangerous man in Germany,” which turned out to be great publicity; at campaign events, he autographed copies of the magazine cover. A fan of Ulrich Siegmund, the lead candidate for the far-right Alternative for Germany, waits for Siegmund to sign copies of Der Spiegel that show him on the cover. (Sean Gallup / Getty) As Siegmund racks up likes on social media, he leaves the most incendiary topics to others in the party. When some members of the state AfD branch traveled to the United States last year to attend a gala of the Trump-aligned New York Young Republican Club, Siegmund stayed home. The party’s ideological engine in Saxony-Anhalt is said to be Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, who has likened Islam to a fungus, condemned the “sacralization of the Holocaust,” and suggested that Jewish institutions are using Muslim immigration to achieve the “abolition of our people.” He has called AIDS patients the “price we pay for a decadent social model” and argued that the Bauhaus movement “raped the human need for comfort.” On foreign policy, Tillschneider sides with Russia in its assault on Ukraine, praising President Vladimir Putin as “a real man with a sound set of values” and insisting that Moscow is “defending itself.” When I asked Tillschneider to explain his party’s success in the region, he said it didn’t stem from one particular issue or another but amounted to a rejection of the mainstream’s whole approach to policy making. He argued that the “established parties have formed a consensus against the interests of the citizens” and refuse to entertain ideas that go against their orthodoxy. The AfD is testing the limits of what’s acceptable in German political culture, especially on immigration. The party’s election manifesto declares ominously, “Our streets and squares are no longer safe.” And it promises a “deportation and remigration offensive.” The term remigration , once a fringe concept linked to ethnic cleansing, is now a focus of far-right immigration discourse, and has flexible meanings. Tillschneider defined it as “the maximum possible deportation within the framework of the constitutional order.” In addition to a “180-degree turn” in migration policy, the party is also vowing to revamp education and art, instill pride in German identity, and end the country’s “guilt complex.” The AfD also objects to the established parties’ anti-Russia policies and seeks to expand Russian-language instruction in schools and revive student exchanges with Russia. The Christian Democrats, who currently govern Saxony-Anhalt in a coalition with the Social Democrats and the liberal Free Democrats, have struggled to respond. The state premier, Sven Schulze, took umbrage at the far right for “constantly belittling Saxony-Anhalt and acting as if everything here is doomed to failure.” AfD representatives can sense the desperation. Tillschneider said the firewall had become a “tomb wall” that the Christian Democratic Union has built for itself. He envisioned only two possibilities after the September election: either an AfD government or an “all-party government against us.” On this there seems to be some agreement. Gürth, the Christian Democratic lawmaker, said his party can’t justify cooperation with the AfD, which “operates like the Nazi Party” in its methods: “It exaggerates real or perceived problems, taps into public discontent, and paints a dystopian picture of Germany teetering on the brink of collapse. All other parties are blamed, and only the AfD can save Germany.” [ Read: J. D. Vance is definitely against foreign election interference ] In the scenario outlined by the Amadeu Antonio Foundation, an AfD-led government soon turns the state into a platform for international self-promotion, hosting conferences and opening offices in Washington and Moscow. Vice President Vance, who met with an AfD leader on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference last year, visits the state and offers to support American companies that choose to invest in Saxony-Anhalt. In the next federal election, in 2029, the AfD wins. The party may soon get the chance to give this scenario a shot.

items.title: Security, traffic plans for Eid Miladun Nabi processions
items.description: Authorities have made elaborate security and road traffic arrangements across the country for rallies in connection with the 12th Rabiul Awwal on Wednesday. Karachi In Karachi, 4,208 policemen have been deployed to secure religious rallies and gatherings in the metropolis, of whom 1,702 have been stationed in South Zone and 765 in East Zone, according to an official statement by police. Police said 397 officers and personnel had been deployed for the security of the main 12th Rabiul Awwal procession at Nishtar Park, and 362 more had been stationed at the entry points of the park. Karachi Additional Inspector General Azad Khan, the metropolis’s police chief, had directed law enforcers to remain on high alert on routes of all processions, and traffic police had been instructed to ensure smooth flow of traffic, the statement said. He also issued directions for the effective monitoring of the security situation through CCTV cameras. Meanwhile, the city’s traffic police said three main processions were planned in the city. The first procession was scheduled to depart from Shaheed Masjid in Kharadar at 2:30pm, pass through Memon Masjid and conclude at Gulzar-i-Habib Mosque at the time of Asr prayers. The second was scheduled to depart from Memon Masjid at 2:30pm and conclude at Aram Bagh Masjid at the time of Asr prayers. The main procession would depart from Memon Masjid after 3pm and conclude at Nishtar Park at around 6pm. Map of procession routes in Karachi — Traffic Police According to the traffic plan for the day, commuters travelling from Nazimabad can proceed towards their destinations from Lasbela Chowk via Nishtar Road towards Garden. Those coming from Liaquatabad can turn left at Teen Hatti and proceed towards Central Jail (Martin Road). Commuters travelling from Hassan Square towards PIB Colony can use Kashmir Road to reach Society Light Signal (Shahrah-i-Quaideen). Those travelling from the Jail Flyover towards Teen Hatti can use Nishtar Road via Lasbela Chowk. No traffic is allowed to travel from the Governor House towards Numaish. Commuters travelling from Sharea Faisal via Shahrah-i-Quaideen (Noorani Kabab) towards Numaish can turn right at Society Light Signal onto Kashmir Road to reach their destinations. Those travelling from Central Jail Gate (Jamshed Road) via Guru Mandir towards M.A. Jinnah Road can use Guru Mandir Bypass Road and Soldier Bazar. Commuters travelling from Garden Chowrangi towards M.A. Jinnah Road can turn right at Anklesaria Hospital towards Gul Plaza, or turn left at Coast Guard/Holy Family Hospital to reach their destinations. Traffic coming from Lucky Star towards M.A. Jinnah Road and Empress Market will be diverted from Saddar Dawakhana towards PP Chowrangi. Similarly, traffic heading towards Preedy Road will be diverted from Abdullah Haroon Road towards M.A. Jinnah Chowk, from where it can proceed towards its destination. Traffic is not allowed to travel from M.A. Jinnah Chowk towards Court Road (Kabootar Chowk). All traffic is to be diverted via Strachan Road towards Pakistan Chowk. Traffic heading from Shahrah-i-Liaquat towards Preedy Road will be diverted from Aram Bagh Light Signal towards Pakistan Chowk, from where it can proceed to its destination. Rawalpindi In Rawalpindi, more than 910 traffic police personnel have been deployed to regulate traffic during the processions. A total of 120 processions will be taken out across the city, including two categorised as A, 10 as B and 108 as C, according to the traffic police. Murree Road will remain closed in both directions during the processions. Traffic travelling from Rawalpindi to Islamabad will be diverted via Tipu Road towards Liaquat Bagh Chowk while vehicles coming from Islamabad will be diverted from the Rawal Road turn towards Rawal Road. Traffic travelling from Liaquat Bagh to Fawara Chowk will be diverted from DAV College towards Gawalmandi. For the second procession, which will start from Chungi No. 22, traffic coming from Kalma Chowk will be diverted towards Harley Street. The procession will pass through Tench Road, Dhoke Syedan Chowk, Kalma Chowk, No. 22 Chowk, Adiala Road, State Life Building turn, MH Chowk, Mahfuz Chowk, Mansehra Adda, Thana Cantt, Nishtar Street, Adamji Road, Mithu Khan Complex, Railway Road, Military Accounts and Kamran Market to conclude at GTS Chowk. Traffic heading towards Khattak Chowk, CMH and Tench will be diverted towards Harley Street during the procession. When the procession reaches Mall Road, traffic coming from Peshawar Road will be diverted from Qasim Market towards Sher Khan Road, the traffic police said. Traffic travelling from Kutchery Chowk towards Peshawar Road will be diverted from TM Chowk to Murree Road. Tractor trolleys, trailers and trucks will not be allowed to enter the procession routes. No parking will be allowed within 300 yards of the stage. A special traffic plan has also been prepared to facilitate ambulances, fire engines and other emergency vehicles. Traffic will be diverted from highways where processions are held, while citizens have been advised to avoid unnecessary travel on procession routes, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Farhan Aslam said. Peshawar The main procession in Peshawar will be held under the banner of Idara Tableeghul Islam. It will start after Isha (night) prayers from Milad Chowk in the city and, after passing through its traditional routes, will culminate at Qissa Khwani Bazaar where the main Mehfil-i-Milad will be held. Several small processions will also be taken out from Sikandar Pura, Qissa Khwani, Saddar, Kohati, Gulbahar and other areas. According to the plan prepared by the city’s traffic police, four superintendents of police, 12 deputy superintendents of police (DSP) and 600 personnel and wardens have been deployed across the city. Citizens can also get traffic updates via helpline 1915. Lahore According to Lahore traffic police, 16 DSPs, 45 sector in-charges and over 1,400 wardens and patrolling officers have been deployed in the city, where two main processions will be taken out. In addition, 172 rallies and 125 Milad gatherings will be organised, the traffic police posted on X. Overall in Punjab, 8,000 traffic police officers and personnel had been deployed across the province, according to a statement by the Punjab traffic police. It said 1,436 Miladun Nabi gatherings and 2,479 processions had been planned across the province, while 216 processions and 111 Milad gatherings would be held in Lahore. The Punjab Police have deployed 55,000 personnel for about 4,500 gatherings and processions across the province for Eid Miladun Nabi. Punjab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Abdul Kareem said that the Counter-Terrorism Department would also monitor the main gatherings other than the field police officers, including regional and district police officers, across the province. He said that security would remain on high alert during the Eid Miladun Nabi programmes.

items.title: Sudan’s Radical Change Forces’ Alliance: Contact with Quintet and UN envoy does not imply external mandate
items.description: Sudan’s Radical Change Forces’ Alliance confirms that it has been in contact with the Quintet initiative (the African Union, the United Nations, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), the League of Arab States, and the European Union) and the office of the UN envoy about Sudan’s political process, but insists that the contacts do not give any external party a mandate to represent it or speak on its behalf. In a statement issued by its foreign relations office on Tuesday, the alliance said its contacts with regional and international parties came as initiatives to address the war in Sudan increased. However, it stressed that Sudan’s future must be determined by the will of the Sudanese people, and that any political settlement should respect Sudan’s sovereignty, unity, and independence of decision-making. The alliance said its contacts with the Quintet and the UN envoy’s office had focused on presenting its views on how the political process should be designed, including who should take part, and how it should proceed. Its position, it said, was that Sudanese people should have full ownership of the political process, while the role of external actors should be limited to facilitating and supporting efforts to reach a sustainable solution. In the statement, seen by Radio Dabanga, the alliance said it had exchanged messages with representatives of the Quintet on 28 July and had sent them documents and memoranda setting out its assessment of the roots of Sudan’s crisis and possible ways out of it. It stressed that contact with external actors did not represent a retreat from its opposition to any settlement that reproduced the forces or policies that, according to the statement, had contributed to the war and the current crisis. Nor did it amount to seeking external legitimacy, it said, but rather provided a means of presenting the alliance’s position to international and regional actors. The alliance welcomed any efforts that could help stop the war, protect civilians, deliver humanitarian assistance, and end violations, as well as ensure justice and accountability. But it warned against using such efforts as a means of imposing political arrangements on the Sudanese people. It said a ceasefire alone would not be enough to end the crisis, and called for a political process that addressed the political, social, economic, and institutional causes that had led to wars and coups. Such a process, it said, should lay the foundations for a democratic civilian state based on the rule of law and equal citizenship, and rebuild state institutions on national and professional foundations. The alliance also called for wider participation in any discussion about Sudan’s future, including representatives of the revolutionary forces, communities affected by the war, women, and young people. It said the political process should not be restricted to armed groups, political elites, and international and regional actors. Ali Mahjoub El Nadif, spokesman for the alliance’s foreign relations office, confirmed that internal and external contacts were continuing, while maintaining what he described as Sudanese independence in decision-making and the right of the Sudanese people to determine the country’s future. Editor’s note: This article has been translated from Arabic with the assistance of artificial intelligence, and subsequently reviewed and adapted by a human editor before publication. items.title: Raheem Sterling charged over Lamborghini crash, nitrous oxide possession
items.description: Former England international Raheem Sterling is set to appear in court next month after being charged with dangerous driving, possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. Sterling, 31, was charged following a single-vehicle crash on the M3 in Hampshire in May. The former Manchester City and Chelsea winger crashed his Lamborghini into motorway barriers near the Minley Interchange on the southbound carriageway on May 28, 2026. He was arrested following the incident and later released on bail pending further investigation. A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesperson said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3. “Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen. “The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange [Hampshire], on 28 May, 2026. “No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported. Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September.” Police had initially suspected Sterling of “driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs”, although that allegation is not among the charges he now faces. Following the crash in May, a source close to Sterling told BBC Sport there was “no proof” that drugs were present in his system. The source also said the footballer had endured “an extremely tough couple of years” and had been made to “feel worthless” and “forgotten about”. Sterling is currently without a club after leaving Feyenoord at the end of last season. He joined the Dutch club on a short-term deal in February after leaving Chelsea by mutual consent. Chelsea had signed Sterling from Manchester City for £47.5m in 2022 following his successful seven-year spell at the Etihad Stadium. During his time at City, Sterling won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and one FA Cup. He subsequently spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal before returning to Chelsea, where he was excluded from the first-team squad and trained separately in 2025. Sterling began his senior career at Liverpool and went on to win 82 England caps between 2012 and 2022. He represented the Three Lions at three World Cups and two European Championships. His court appearance at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court is scheduled for September 15. items.title: «Dégâts sans précédent» : les frappes iraniennes infligent des milliards de dollars de dommages aux sites de renseignement américains au Moyen-Orient
items.description: Selon un reportage exclusif de NBC News publie ce 25 août, les frappes iraniennes ont inflige aux postes de renseignement et au materiel de surveillance des etats-Unis dans la region un niveau de destruction superieur a tout ce que les agences d'espionnage americaines avaient connu jusqu'ici. Des infrastructures de la CIA et d'autres services durement touchees Quatre sources informees citees par la chaîne americaine indiquent que les bâtiments et les equipements de collecte de renseignements par la CIA et d'autres agences ont ete endommages. Le montant des reparations ou du remplacement se chiffre en milliards de dollars. « L'ampleur de la destruction est decrite comme depassant tous les dommages subis precedemment par les agences de renseignement americaines », rapportent ces sources. NBC: "Iran has inflicted unprecedented damage to US facilities in the Middle East." According to NBC, Iranian missile strikes and drone attacks have caused damage to US intelligence outposts and surveillance equipment in the Middle East, exceeding the scale of any destruction… pic.twitter.com/jYxDHEfp91 — 𝕊𝕡𝕣𝕚𝕟𝕥𝕖𝕣 𝕻𝕣𝕖𝕤𝕤 (@SprinterPress) August 26, 2026 Parmi les sites mentionnes dans les comptes rendus figurent la station de la CIA a Riyad, touchee par des drones en mars, ainsi qu'une installation dans la province de Sulaymaniyah en Irak, frappee en debut de conflit. Des systemes de radar et d'autres materiels partages entre le Pentagone et les services de renseignement ont egalement ete atteints dans plusieurs pays de la region. Les tensions se sont intensifiees depuis les frappes conjointes americano-israeliennes contre l'Iran en fevrier 2026. Teheran a repondu par des attaques contre les interets americains heberges dans des pays allies a Washington . Plus de 2 000 frappes iraniennes de missiles, drones et aeriens ont vise au moins 20 sites gouvernementaux americains dans huit pays. Un memorandum d'entente signe a la mi-juin sous mediation pakistanaise visait a mettre fin aux hostilites. Les discussions ont toutefois echoue sur les termes de l'accord et la libre navigation dans le detroit d'Ormuz. Dans ce contexte, le vice-ministre des Affaires etrangeres, Gharibabadi, a mis en garde les etats-Unis contre toute nouvelle agression et menace d'utiliser des moyens militaires jusqu'alors non utilises. ⚠️ IRAN ESCALATES RHETORIC OVER NEW CAPABILITIES 🇮🇷 Deputy FM Gharibabadi warns the US against further aggression, threatening to unveil undisclosed military assets. Tensions spike amid volatile maritime activity near the STRAIT OF HORMUZ. 🚢📡 #IRAN #OSINT — OSN - Observer Security Network (@OSN_Reports) August 26, 2026 Le Congres doit desormais trouver des fonds pour restaurer les installations touchees, tandis que les responsables americains reevaluent le deploiement du personnel et des ressources de renseignement dans une zone exposee aux drones et missiles iraniens. Des experts, comme Seth Jones du Center for Strategic and International Studies , soulignent que la guerre a revele des lacunes dans la defense des bases americaines. Un echec militaire qui semble pousser Donald Trump a se diriger vers une guerre economique avec Teheran en tentant d'isoler le pays .

items.title: ‘We don’t work with visa agents’ — German Embassy warns Nigerians
items.description: The German Embassy in Nigeria has warned visa applicants against relying on so-called “visa agents” for information about travelling to Germany. In a recent tweet, the embassy urged Nigerians to be cautious about information provided by individuals claiming to have special knowledge or access to the German visa process. The embassy said applicants should verify visa-related information directly with the German mission rather than relying on claims from visa agents. “Beware of misinformation. Save yourself the hassle & just ask us directly,” the embassy said. It also asked Nigerians to share some of the claims they had heard from “visa agents” in the comments, saying it would address them in upcoming posts. The German mission made its position on visa agents clear, stating: “We DO NOT WORK with any ‘Visa Agents’!” The embassy added that applicants do not need to depend on agents to access official information, as details about German visas and application procedures are freely available through its website. The warning comes as many Nigerians seeking to travel to Germany rely on third parties for assistance with visa applications, including tourism, study, employment and family reunification. The embassy’s clarification means applicants should be wary of anyone claiming to represent the German Embassy or suggesting that they have special influence over visa decisions. Official German visa information for applicants in Nigeria is available through the German Missions in Nigeria. items.title: Référendum sur l’Europe : un poisson nommé Islande
items.description: Ce 29 août 2026, les Islandais sont appelés aux urnes pour un référendum sur la réouverture d’un processus d’adhésion à l’Union européenne (UE), interrompu depuis plus d’une décennie. Le scrutin est consultatif, même si le gouvernement s’est engagé à en respecter le résultat. Si le « oui » l’emporte, de nouvelles négociations seraient engagées et un accord final d’adhésion devrait ensuite être soumis aux Islandais. À quelques jours du vote, les sondages témoignent d’un pays profondément partagé, illustrant un dilemme de souveraineté et de puissance. Il s’agit aussi, en miroir, d’une potentielle réflexion stratégique à venir pour l’UE : est-elle capable de développer une nouvelle ambition maritime et halieutique si l’Islande intègre la Communauté ? Points de repère spatio-temporels Sur une carte, l’Islande semble périphérique, avec à peine moins d’un demi-million d’habitants sur cette île volcanique de l’Atlantique Nord. Mais sur une carte océanique, elle trouve davantage de centralité, avec une position charnière entre Europe, Amérique du Nord et Arctique. Tout le paradoxe géopolitique islandais est là : petite puissance terrestre et démographique, mais grande puissance maritime et halieutique. La Chine ne s’y trompe d’ailleurs pas, souhaitant placer des pions en Islande dans le cadre de sa stratégie des routes polaires de la soie. L’Islande est déjà profondément imbriquée dans l’espace européen. Membre fondateur de l’Organisation du traité de l’Atlantique Nord (OTAN) en 1949, elle appartient à l’Association européenne de libre-échange depuis 1970, à l’Espace économique européen (EEE) depuis 1994 et à l’espace Schengen depuis 2001. Elle applique ainsi une partie considérable des règles du marché intérieur européen et participe à de nombreux programmes sans être membre de l’UE. Son économie est également très connectée au continent. Cette proximité économique et institutionnelle rend parfois difficile à percevoir ce qui sépare encore véritablement Reykjavik de Bruxelles. Or, deux secteurs essentiels restent précisément à l’écart du fonctionnement ordinaire de l’EEE : l’agriculture et la pêche. Ce n’est évidemment pas anodin. L’une des singularités de l’Islande réside dans la place occupée par ses ressources naturelles et surtout marines. Sa prospérité, son histoire et une partie de son identité se sont construites autour de cette mer nourricière. L’Islande avait officiellement déposé sa candidature à l’UE en 2009, dans le contexte de la grave crise financière internationale, qui n’avait pas épargné le pays. Les négociations furent suspendues en 2013, avant que le processus ne soit abandonné en 2015. Parmi les principaux points de friction figurait déjà la pêche. Plus d’une décennie après, le contexte global a changé, avec notamment ces velléités trumpiennes sur le Groenland qui perturbent les raisonnements islandais et modifient les enjeux dans l’Arctique pour l’UE. Or, si l’Islande et l’UE peuvent trouver de nouvelles raisons géopolitiques à se rapprocher, la pêche reste l’épine dorsale des divisions. La singularité halieutique islandaise La pêche et l’aquaculture représentent environ 7 % du PIB, 5 % de l’emploi et près de 40 % des exportations islandaises de marchandises. Les captures atteignent en moyenne 1,4 million de tonnes par an, dont environ 710 000 tonnes d’espèces démersales – parmi lesquelles quelque 220 000 tonnes de morue – et 550 000 tonnes de poissons pélagiques comme le capelan, le maquereau ou le hareng. L’aquaculture progresse, notamment en saumon. Il faut dire que de nombreux pays de l’UE en raffolent (à commencer par la France) sans en produire sur leurs littoraux ou leurs sols. Parler d’une éventuelle adhésion de l’Islande à l’Union européenne sans parler de poisson reviendrait presque à parler de l’Arabie saoudite sans évoquer le pétrole. Car la pêche islandaise n’est pas une activité économique périphérique qu’il faudrait maintenir artificiellement en vie. Au contraire, les Islandais en sont fiers et misent sur ce secteur. Ce dernier s’avère créateur de richesses, exportateur, performant et fortement intégré aux circuits mondiaux. Sa ressource sauvage – cabillaud, églefin, espèces pélagiques notamment – comme sa production aquacole sont très recherchées sur des marchés où la concurrence est mondiale. Les produits islandais sont largement présents sur le marché européen. Les opérateurs se sont adaptés au Brexit, avec notamment un redéploiement d’une partie des flux vers les Pays-Bas avant redistribution vers d’autres États membres. L’Islande dispose donc déjà du débouché européen sans appartenir à l’UE. La pêche en Islande, attribut de souveraineté Entre les années 1950 et 1970, les fameuses « guerres de la morue » opposèrent l’Islande au Royaume-Uni autour de l’extension des zones de pêche islandaises. Reykjavik parvint progressivement à imposer son contrôle jusqu’à 200 milles nautiques de ses côtes. Pour cette micro-nation insulaire, la maîtrise de la mer et de ses ressources est ainsi devenue une manifestation particulièrement concrète de l’indépendance nationale. Cette mémoire demeure présente. Là où d’autres États pensent leur souveraineté d’abord à travers leurs frontières terrestres, l’Islande la pense aussi à travers ses poissons, ses quotas, ses navires et son espace maritime. Et c’est ici la tension majeure d’une éventuelle adhésion à l’UE : pour la pêche islandaise, l’intérêt à y entrer reste faible. Pour Reykjavik, la question est d’abord celle de la souveraineté. L’Islande détermine largement ses règles de gestion des ressources halieutiques et défend jalousement le contrôle de ses stocks, de ses quotas et de l’accès à ses eaux. Une éventuelle adhésion obligerait pourtant l’Islande à négocier son intégration à la politique commune de la pêche (PCP). Les modalités feraient évidemment l’objet de discussions, mais le principe est politiquement explosif : pourquoi transférer une partie de sa capacité de décision à Bruxelles sur une ressource considérée comme nationale, stratégique et particulièrement bien valorisée ? Pourquoi modifier un modèle qui fonctionne, accepter davantage de règles communes et renoncer à une partie d’autonomie alors que l’accès au marché européen existe déjà ? Si pour Bruxelles, la pêche pourrait constituer l’une des raisons de vouloir l’Islande dans l’Union, pour une partie du secteur halieutique islandais, elle constitue précisément l’une des meilleures raisons de rester dehors. Entrer dans l’UE en rejetant le poisson ? Soyons réalistes : la PCP ne fait pas rêver Reykjavik. Cette évaluation est d’autant plus légitime que la pêche européenne traverse elle-même de fortes tensions et que l’UE peine à définir un cap clair en matière de stratégie halieutique. Rappelons ici que les produits de la mer font partie des plus grandes dépendances alimentaires dans la majorité des pays de l’UE. Cela vaut pour la France, grande puissance bleue, sauf dans l’assiette. Depuis plusieurs décennies, la PCP cherche à concilier trois impératifs : exploiter économiquement les ressources, assurer le renouvellement des stocks et protéger les écosystèmes marins. Quotas, limitations de l’effort de pêche, contraintes pesant sur les capacités des flottes (coût de l’énergie, vieillissement des professionnels, etc.), développement des aires marines protégées et multiplication des normes environnementales alimentent chez une partie des pêcheurs européens le sentiment d’un espace halieutique qui se rétrécit. La flotte européenne diminue et sa vétuste inquiète. Certains armateurs connaissent de sérieuses difficultés économiques, d’autant que la compétition internationale s’est intensifiée. L’UE veut protéger ses zones maritimes, mais elle importe donc massivement les produits de la mer qu’elle consomme. Réduire la pression de pêche dans les eaux européennes peut produire un bénéfice environnemental local. Mais si la consommation demeure et si elle est satisfaite par davantage d’importations, la pression productive ne disparaît pas nécessairement. Elle peut aussi être déplacée vers d’autres mers. La question ne serait-elle pas de déterminer comment l’Europe peut simultanément préserver ses ressources et préserver sa capacité à produire ? Cela pourrait être le narratif islandais, d’autant que l’on voit mal ce pays ne pas rester une puissance halieutique quand bien même l’adhésion à l’UE se profilerait. Dit autrement, Reykjavik pourrait-elle faire évoluer la PCP et la vision halieutique de l’UE ? Se tourner vers l’avenir Le Brexit a rétréci l’Europe maritime, l’Islande pourrait l’agrandir. La sortie du Royaume-Uni en 2020 a accéléré les problématiques pour les pêcheries européennes. L’hypothèse d’une intégration de l’Islande dans l’UE pourrait rebattre les cartes, une décennie plus tard. La zone économique exclusive islandaise représente environ 758 000 km². Son adhésion accroîtrait donc considérablement l’espace maritime relevant d’un État membre de l’UE. Les captures islandaises représentent à elles seules l’équivalent d’environ 30 % des volumes actuellement pêchés par l’UE27. Avec l’Islande, l’UE réaliserait 5 % des captures mondiales. Aujourd’hui, l’Islande est simultanément partenaire et redoutable concurrent halieutique de l’Union européenne. Sa flotte est productive, son expertise scientifique reconnue, son industrie de transformation performante et son système de gestion des ressources fortement structuré. Avec la Norvège, elle illustre une forme de puissance halieutique nordique fondée sur l’association entre ressources, technologie, efficacité des flottes et gestion des stocks. Tant qu’elle reste extérieure à l’UE, cette puissance s’exerce en partie face à elle : compétition commerciale, négociations sur les stocks partagés, accès aux marchés, quotas et rapports de force autour des espèces migratoires. Mais l’adhésion changerait la perspective. L’Islande intégrée pourrait devenir une contributrice majeure à la capacité halieutique et alimentaire européenne. À une condition cependant : que l’UE souhaite redevenir une puissance halieutique et s’assume comme protagoniste sur les affaires maritimes de l’Arctique. C’est là que le référendum islandais devient un débat européen si le oui l’emporte le 28 août et si le processus d’adhésion s’en trouve relancé. L’UE transformera l’Islande, mais l’Islande pourrait aussi faire évoluer l’Europe halieutique. Il ne s’agirait évidemment pas de revenir sur la nécessité d’une gestion durable des ressources. Une puissance halieutique ne peut l’être durablement qu’en préservant le capital biologique sur lequel elle repose. Mais soutenabilité et puissance ne sont pas nécessairement contradictoires. Sous cet angle, un parallèle peut être esquissé avec l’Ukraine agricole, qui apporterait des forces considérables à l’UE dans ce secteur en cas d’adhésion de Kiev demain, si et seulement si une vision géopolitique et géoéconomique s’exprime. Sans cela, l’agriculture constituera le dossier le plus explosif et le plus fracturant du dialogue euro-ukrainien. Les situations sont évidemment très différentes par leur taille, leur histoire et leur contexte géopolitique. Mais elles interrogent toutes deux la manière dont l’Union envisage ses futurs élargissements Ukraine et Islande posent ainsi, chacune dans leur domaine, une même question à Bruxelles : l’élargissement consiste-t-il seulement à étendre un espace juridique et réglementaire, ou peut-il aussi servir à agréger de nouvelles capacités de puissance ? Quand les poissons déplacent la géopolitique Ajoutons une brique aux réflexions précédentes. La question euro-islandaise devient encore plus stratégique avec le changement climatique. Le réchauffement des eaux modifie progressivement la répartition géographique de certaines espèces. Les stocks évoluent, migrent ou deviennent plus variables. Certaines espèces apparaissent davantage dans certaines zones tandis qu’elles en délaissent d’autres. La géographie de la pêche n’est donc pas immuable. Les tensions observées autour du maquereau entre l’Islande, les îles Féroé, la Norvège et l’UE en fournissent une illustration. Elles pourraient préfigurer d’autres controverses à mesure que le changement climatique transforme les écosystèmes de l’Atlantique Nord. Un poisson qui change de latitude peut déplacer de la valeur économique, chambouler des quotas et durcir des discussions diplomatiques. La gouvernance halieutique devient ainsi une forme de géopolitique climatique. Elle oblige les États côtiers à négocier simultanément la conservation de ressources mobiles, l’accès aux zones de pêche et le partage de la richesse qu’elles génèrent. Cette évolution renforce mécaniquement la valeur stratégique des États disposant à la fois d’importants espaces maritimes, d’une expertise scientifique reconnue et d’une industrie halieutique performante. L’Islande réunit précisément ces trois caractéristiques. La mer pousse l’Islande à préserver son autonomie ; la géopolitique peut la pousser vers l’UE. Contrairement à la Norvège, l’Islande ne dispose pas de la même profondeur financière et énergétique pour absorber les chocs d’un environnement international plus incertain. Dans un monde où les rapports de force reviennent au premier plan, la petite taille démographique peut redevenir une vulnérabilité. La campagne référendaire conduit naturellement les Islandais à s’interroger sur ce que l’UE pourrait leur apporter : sécurité, influence politique, stabilité économique ou perspective d’intégration monétaire. La dynamique géopolitique en Arctique pousse au rapprochement avec l’UE. Mais la souveraineté halieutique les invite à la prudence. Mais il convient de poser aussi la question de ce que gagnerait l’UE avec l’Islande. Dans cette perspective, le sujet halieutique, avec ses composantes spatio-maritimes et économico-alimentaires, est inévitable. L’article Référendum sur l’Europe : un poisson nommé Islande est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.description: Le poste de péage de Ouaga-route de Pô, à Koubri, a changé d’emplacement. L’Agence de Gestion du Péage (AGP) l’a annoncé dans une note d’information publiée le 25 août 2026. Le nouveau site, situé à l’extérieur de la voie de contournement, est opérationnel depuis ce même mardi, à partir de 8 heures. Désormais, les usagers de la Route nationale 5 doivent s’acquitter de leurs droits de péage à cet endroit. Le poste se trouve à proximité du rond-point menant à Koubri. Pour les automobilistes venant de Koubri, la barrière est placée à l’entrée du rond-point. Ceux qui se rendent à Koubri paieront à la sortie. Selon l’AGP, ce déplacement répond à trois objectifs : renforcer la sécurité des usagers, améliorer la fluidité du trafic et optimiser le recouvrement des recettes. L’agence invite les conducteurs et transporteurs à respecter scrupuleusement la signalisation installée sur place. items.description: Tchamba, 25 août (ATOP) – Le préfet de Tchamba, Issaka Laguebande, et le maire de la commune Tchamba 1, Hamza Titikpina, ont effectué, le lundi 24 août, une tournée dans plusieurs centres d’enregistrement biométrique de la ville. La tournée s’est déroulée dans plusieurs centres notamment l’EPP Centrale, EPP Watouwa, EPP Larini, au Complexe Jean-Paul II et à l’EPP Iyiwa. L’objectif de cette descente est de constater l’affluence et s’assurer que toutes les dispositions sont prises pour faciliter le recensement des citoyens. Le préfet et le maire ont félicité les agents recenseurs pour la qualité du travail accompli depuis le lancement de l’opération le 21 août. Ils ont invité les agents à faire preuve de patience, d’écoute et de vigilance afin que personne ne soit laissé de côté. Les deux autorités ont insisté sur la prise en charge prioritaire des personnes âgées et des personnes vivant avec un handicap. Elles ont rappelé que l’opération est gratuite et ouverte à tous, sans distinction puis exhorté la population à respecter les directives des agents et à sensibiliser les voisins à venir se faire enrôler. Cette opération se poursuit jusqu’au 21 septembre dans la préfecture de Tchamba. ATOP/SA/MEK/BA

items.title: Cameroun : l’UDC se préoccupe de la qualité des résultats attendus du 4e Recensement général de la population
items.description: © DR Au vu des difficultés opérationnelles du dénombrement et des renvois successifs de la fin de l’opération sur le terrain, la présidente de l'Union démocratique du Cameroun interpelle le gouvernement, les partenaires et les populations non encore recensées. La qualité des résultats attendus au terme du 4e Recensement général de la population et de l'habitat couplé au Recensement général de l'agriculture et de l'élevage préoccupe l'Union démocratique du Cameroun (UDC). La présidente du parti, le maire Patricia Tomaino Ndam Njoya exprime sa préoccupation dans une déclaration rendue publique le 23 aout dernier. Motivée par le double renvoi de l'échéance prévue pour la fin du dénombrement ainsi que par les cinq années passées pour publier les résultats du 3eme Recensement effectué en 2005, la femme politique s'interroge. Elle se pose des questions sur l'efficacité et la performance du système. Ainsi que sur la volonté de rendre publique les statistiques fidèles. Lancée le 24 avril 2026, l'opération va s'étendre jusqu'au 15 septembre. A terme, elle aura duré cinq mois. Pourtant, en 2021, la Côte d'Ivoire a recensé près de 30 millions d'habitants en cinq semaines. La préoccupation amène ainsi le leader politique à lancer un appel aux gouvernants et aux partenaires. L'ancienne députée propose de rendre plus inclusive le dénombrement. De s'assurer que les agents recenseurs perçoivent la totalité de leurs indemnités. De déterminer des points fixes où les populations encore non recensées peuvent le faire. Pour la crédibilité de l’opération, Tomaino Ndam Njoya demande aussi au gouvernement d'élaborer un chronogramme d'activités à respecter pour la centralisation des résultats. Aux populations qui traînent le pas, l'UDC appelle à faire un effort. Pour le parti, le recensement n'est pas une campagne politique. C'est une opération visant à actualiser les données de la population, de l'habitat, de l'agriculture, de l'élevage, en vue de favoriser la prise de décisions stratégiques, socio-économiques, politiques et institutionnelles. Après son lancement en avril pour se terminer le 29 mai, le recensement se poursuit à la faveur de deux prolongations. La première décidée par le Premier ministre le 29 mai prévoyait la fin des opérations le 31 juillet. Le même jour, le chef du gouvernement décide d'une nouvelle prorogation fixant la fin du recensement au 15 septembre. Les activités en cours visent à recenser 40% de la population restante. Cet article Cameroun : l'UDC se préoccupe de la qualité des résultats attendus du 4e Recensement général de la population est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Un crocodile dans un étang à Adéticopé : les populations appelées à faire preuve de vigilance
items.description: Lomé, 26 août (ATOP) – A travers un communiqué en date du mardi 25 août, le maire de la commune Agoè-Nyivé 6, Songhoi Kézié, informe la population d’Adétikopé qu’un crocodile a été signalé dans un étang situé derrière la Gendarmerie de la localité. Il est également interdit d’exercer toute activité aux abords immédiats de ce site. Le maire invite la population, notamment les parents, les enfants, les jeunes, les pécheurs et toutes les personnes ayant l’habitude de fréquenter cette zone, à faire preuve de vigilance et à se conformer aux exigences de sécurité. La population est invitée à en informer immédiatement les autorités compétentes car un crocodile reste un animal dangereux et protégé. ATOP/BA/AJA

items.title: Poco Lee’s management breaks silence, denies drink-spiking claims
items.description: The management of Nigerian dancer and singer Poco Lee has broken its silence on the sexual assault case involving the entertainer in the United Kingdom. In a statement issued on Tuesday, August 25, the dancer’s management confirmed that the matter is currently before a UK court and urged the public to allow the legal process to take its course. The team cautioned against treating the allegations as established facts, stressing that Poco Lee has not been convicted of any offence. “Allegations are not evidence of guilt, and no conclusions should be drawn until the matter has been heard and determined through the appropriate legal process,” the statement said. The management also addressed reports circulating online about alleged drink-spiking, clarifying that such claims are not contained in the allegations currently before the court. “We ask the public and media to desist from introducing details that are not part of the actual case, as doing so only fuels misinformation and causes unfair prejudice to all parties involved,” the statement added. Reports of Poco Lee’s arrest in the UK emerged on August 19, with reports linking his detention to a sexual assault allegation. At the time, details surrounding the case, including the identity of the alleged victim and the circumstances of the incident, were not publicly established by British authorities. Amid the reports, a Texas-based Nigerian rapper, Ms Jorji, also made separate allegations against Poco Lee in videos shared online. She claimed that he attempted to sexually assault her and her girlfriend about two years ago during a visit to his home in Dallas. However, her allegations have not been independently verified by a court or law enforcement agency, and no connection has been established between her claims and the ongoing UK case. Poco Lee, whose real name is Iweh Pascal Odinaka, rose to prominence after appearing in Zlatan Ibile’s “Zanku (Legwork)” music video in 2018. He has since become one of Nigeria’s prominent dancers and entertainers, working with several leading artistes, including Davido, Burna Boy, Olamide and Naira Marley. His management said further updates on the case would be communicated through official channels and appealed to the public to exercise patience and restraint while the legal proceedings continue. items.title: Les Douanes algériennes déploient 14 postes de surveillance aux frontières : leurs missions
items.description: L’Algérie multiplie les mesures pour renforcer les contrôles aux frontières. Après le déploiement d’agents du ministère du Commerce intérieur spécialisés dans la répression des fraudes et le contrôle de la qualité des produits, les Douanes algériennes ajoutent une couche supplémentaire à leur dispositif de surveillance. Une décision datée du 1er juin 2026 portant création des postes de douane de surveillance vient d’entrer en vigueur après sa publication au Journal officiel n°60. Le poste de douane de surveillance est « l'unité structurelle implantée au niveau des frontières terrestres », précise l’article 2 de la décision signée par le directeur général des Douanes algériennes, Abdelhafid Bekhouche. Postes de douane de surveillance aux frontières : voici leurs implantations et leurs missions L’article 3 du même texte a fixé les lieux d’implantation et les missions de ces postes : Assurer une surveillance continue au niveau de la bande frontalière adjacente Apporter le soutien opérationnel aux différentes brigades opérationnelles des douanes, dans la limite de la compétence territoriale Assurer une coordination permanente avec les unités de la gendarmerie nationale compétentes, dans la limite de la compétence territoriale, dans le cadre de la lutte contre toute forme de criminalité transfrontalière Veiller à la sécurité des personnels et des biens au niveau des postes des douanes de surveillance Veiller à la sécurité des marchandises saisies jusqu’à leur remise au receveur des douanes compétent. Au total, 14 postes de surveillance ont été créés par les Douanes algériennes à Tlemcen (05), Naâma (03), Maghnia (02) et Souk Ahras (04). items.title: Presidential campaign council list to be adjusted, not reviewed — Presidency
items.description: By Bayo Wahab The Presidency has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council list for the 2027 election will be adjusted where necessary, but denied that the list has been withdrawn or subjected to a wholesale review. Sunday Dare, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Public Communication, made this known on Wednesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . Dare was responding to reports that the APC had withdrawn the list following controversy over the inclusion and exclusion of some party leaders and other political figures. He said the list remained valid, stressing that the party was yet to constitute all the subcommittees that would make up the campaign structure. “As it is with every other list, there’s a room for subcommittees. Those subcommittees have not been formed, and so many other names will come into that subcommittee,” Dare said. “So that list has not been withdrawn. The APC has issued a statement to that effect yesterday, that list stands. But of course, there will be adjustments. The list is not cast in stone, just like every other list.” The APC had on Tuesday rejected reports that its 2027 presidential campaign council list had been withdrawn. The list, announced over the weekend, named President Tinubu as chairman of the council, with Vice-President Kashim Shettima and APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda as vice chairmen. Former Zamfara State Governor and Senator, Abdul’aziz Yari, was named Director-General, while Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma was designated secretary. Asked whether the list was therefore open to review, Dare avoided the term “review”, describing the expected changes instead as adjustments. “Not a review, just adjustments where necessary,” he said. When pressed on whether his reluctance to use the word “review” meant the list was indeed being reconsidered, the presidential aide maintained that the expected changes did not amount to a comprehensive overhaul. “Review is wholesale, this is not wholesale,” Dare said. He explained that the creation of additional subcommittees would provide room for more party members and political stakeholders to participate in the campaign structure. items.title: Yari’s 2031 Declaration: CSOs, lawyers, others reject APC’s claim to perpetual power
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu, ABUJA Civil society organisations, lawyers and opposition politicians have dismissed the declaration by the Director-General of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’Aziz Yari, that the ruling party will remain in power beyond 2031, saying political power belongs to the electorate and not any political party. Read Also: Highways of horror: Motorists wail, spend 4 days on Benin-Asaba road The groups warned that while the APC was entitled to aspire to retain power, predicting electoral victories years ahead could create a dangerous impression of political entitlement, undermine confidence in elections and discourage citizens from participating in the democratic process. They spoke against the backdrop of Yari’s recent declaration that the APC would continue governing Nigeria beyond 2031. Executive Director of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre, CISLAC, Auwal Rafsanjani, described Yari’s position as “an expression of partisan optimism”, insisting that it must not be presented as though future electoral outcomes had already been determined. Rafsanjani said: “The Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre, CISLAC, considers the declaration by the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’Aziz Yari, that the APC will continue to govern Nigeria beyond 2031 as an expression of partisan optimism, but one that must not be presented as if Nigeria’s future electoral outcomes have already been decided and determined. “In a democracy, however, no political party has a permanent entitlement to power. The authority to determine who governs Nigeria in 2027, 2031 or any subsequent election belongs exclusively to Nigerian voters through credible, competitive, free and fair elections.” The CISLAC boss warned that such utterances could undermine Nigerians’ confidence in the electoral process, describing it as careless to make statements suggesting predetermined electoral victories ahead of the 2027 general elections. Osun poll, a reality check Rafsanjani urged the APC and other political parties not to overlook the lessons of the recent Osun State governorship election, saying the outcome demonstrated that Nigerian voters could not be taken for granted. “The recent Osun State governorship election provides an important reality check for every political party, including the APC,” he said. According to him, “This election demonstrates clearly that Nigerian voters cannot simply be taken for granted. “Even a governing party with substantial political structures, influential personalities and access to significant campaign machinery can be defeated where voters decide otherwise. “Therefore, the Osun election does not support the assumption that any political party can confidently predict that it will remain in power until or beyond 2031. “Rather, it demonstrates that electoral power ultimately rests with citizens when their votes are allowed to count.” He said political parties should focus less on declarations of prolonged rule and more on addressing the problems confronting Nigerians. “Instead of political leaders making declarations about ruling Nigeria for another several years, CISLAC believes attention should be directed towards the urgent concerns confronting ordinary Nigerians. “Nigerians will judge political parties and candidates based on their ability to address insecurity, unemployment, poverty, inflation and the cost of living, corruption, deteriorating public services and citizens’ confidence in governance institutions.” Rafsanjani added that the governing party should allow its performance to determine whether Nigerians would renew its mandate. “Political dominance should not be achieved through incumbency advantage, manipulation of electoral institutions, intimidation of opposition parties, vote-buying, abuse of state resources or weakening of democratic institutions. It should come only through the freely expressed mandate of citizens. “CISLAC urges not only the APC but every political party participating in the 2027 elections to understand that Nigeria belongs to its citizens, not to any particular party.” He advised political parties to base their campaigns on programmes, ideas and records rather than predictions of victory. “Campaigns should therefore focus on ideas, programmes, track records and solutions, rather than declarations suggesting predetermined electoral victories,” he said. The CISLAC director also charged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, security agencies and other state institutions to remain neutral. “The responsibility of INEC, security agencies and other state institutions is equally important. They must remain politically neutral and ensure that no political party—whether governing or opposition—is given an unfair advantage.” He stressed that Yari and the APC had the right to seek continued control of government, but could not claim ownership of the future. “Senator Yari and the APC are entitled to aspire to remain in government beyond 2031, just as opposition parties are entitled to aspire to replace them. But aspiration must never be confused with entitlement. “Ultimately, 2031 belongs neither to APC nor to any opposition party. It belongs to the Nigerian people. The ballot, not political declarations, must determine who governs Nigeria.” ‘Yari disregards electorate’ Human rights lawyer, Idris Faro, also faulted Yari’s declaration, saying electoral victory was determined by voters and not pronouncements by politicians. “Electoral victory is ordinarily determined by the programmes and policies implemented by a political party. It is not determined by an unguarded statement of a politician. “To assert that your party will rule beyond 2031 shows that you have no regard for the role and power of the electorate,” Faro stated. He said a politician confident in his party’s performance should point to achievements and allow voters to make the final judgment. “A careful politician would state that with the number of transport infrastructure done, economic reforms introduced which have stabilised the economy, and constitutional amendments passed, he believes his party will win future elections.” Faro added: “Historical evidence runs contrary to that reckless assertion. Your hope ought to be based on the appreciation of your projects and scores given by the voters.” Nigerians’ll decide — ActionAid Country Director, ActionAid Nigeria, Dr Andrew Mamedu, said no government or political party could guarantee victory in 2027 or any subsequent election because the ultimate power rested with Nigerians. “For us in civil society, we insist that there should be free, fair and credible elections so that the votes of the people, the voice of the people is what matters, what counts at the end of the day,” Mamedu said. “So a particular administration cannot, nobody can say for certain that they will win this election, win the next election. “From what Senator Yari has said, it means that they will win this coming election and win the next one, but that’s not for him to say, that’s not for him to decide. “It is left for the people of Nigeria to decide, it’s left for the citizens of Nigeria and that majority of the citizens to decide. So people should come out and cast their vote.” Mamedu, however, said Yari’s statement could also be interpreted as a challenge to the APC to improve its performance. “On the other hand, it could mean that APC, of course, would need to sit up from what they are doing right now. “There are clear indications that people are still feeling the hardship, people are still feeling, are still looking for more good governance from all across, from both federal and states, across board.” According to him, the ruling party could retain power if it performed better and implemented policies that improved citizens’ welfare. “So it could mean that APC, Senator Yari, is saying that the APC is going to sit up and do better, that’s another way to interpret it, that if they do better, if they implement pro-poor policies, policies that concern the people, positively affect the people, then of course people will vote them in and vote them back.” He, however, warned against any interpretation suggesting that the APC intended to retain power through illegitimate means. “Or it could also mean that they are thinking that they will come in and they would do that by all means possible. Could that also mean that they would want to get into power by all means possible, including doing things that are illegitimate or illegal? ‘Don’t be frightened’ Mamedu said Yari was speaking as a politician and urged Nigerians not to be discouraged from voting by declarations of predetermined victory. “But what would you expect from a politician? That’s a politician speaking like a politician but definitely for us in civil society, we do not, of course we do not subscribe to that. “We clearly say that people should come out, elections have not been held, so results have not been declared. So what he has said should not frighten people.” He said such declarations could create voter apathy if citizens believed that election outcomes had already been decided. “You hear people saying, ‘oh, what is it, come out for election. It’s like, oh, there’s no need to come out. Why? Because they have already decided to vote’. “Who has decided to vote? There’s a fear from some people thinking that, ‘oh, the results will be manipulated, so why bother to come out?’ But the more people come out, like has been demonstrated in some elections, I think Osun is a perfect example. “The more people come out, the more it is difficult for elections to be rigged, elections to be manipulated, and then the will of the people will count.” Don’t mistake incumbency for permanent power — BOOT Party National Chairman of the Because Of Our Tomorrow, BOOT Party, Sonny Adenuga, warned the APC against confusing its incumbency advantage with an entitlement to remain in power indefinitely. Adenuga said political history was replete with examples of parties that once appeared invincible but eventually lost power. “When a ruling party chieftain speaks with such certainty about remaining in power beyond 2031, it reflects more arrogance than political foresight. “We have heard such declarations before. Senator Mantu once confidently proclaimed that the PDP would rule Nigeria for 60 years. History, of course, had a different script.” He advised the APC to learn from history and avoid assuming that its present dominance would automatically translate into future electoral victories. “The APC should therefore be careful not to confuse the advantages of incumbency with an entitlement to permanent power. “Its greatest political asset today is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What happens after Tinubu will be a different political contest, and I believe many within the APC who have the foresight to look beyond today are already preparing for the post-Tinubu era.” Adenuga stressed that democracy could not guarantee any party perpetual control of government. “Democracy does not guarantee any political party perpetual ownership of power. “Ultimately, it is the Nigerian people who decide who governs them, and their choice can never be taken for granted.” He concluded with a warning that political fortunes could change rapidly. “I wish the Campaign DG well. Let them ride and enjoy the tide while it lasts. But in politics, tides change, and no party should mistake today’s dominance for tomorrow’s destiny.” Vanguard News The post Yari’s 2031 Declaration: CSOs, lawyers, others reject APC’s claim to perpetual power appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La légende de la country Dolly Parton s’éteint à 80 ans
items.description: La légende américaine de la musique country Dolly Parton, inoubliable interprète de « Jolene » et « figure fédératrice » à la popularité immense, s'est éteinte à 80 ans mardi, suscitant une intense vague d'émotion. « Elle a toujours été présente sur votre télévision, votre tourne-disque, vos CD ou dans la playlist de votre téléphone, devenant un membre à part entière de votre famille », a déclaré son neveu dans une vidéo annonçant son décès, diffusée sur les réseaux sociaux de la star.La famille de la chanteuse n'a pas précisé la cause de sa mort, mais les médias américains, citant des représentants de l'artiste, ont rapporté qu'elle était décédée après « un bref combat contre le cancer ». Signe de l'émotion qui a saisi l'Amérique, Donald Trump a ordonné de mettre les drapeaux en berne pour une semaine et regretté une « vraie perte pour des millions de personnes ». Son prédécesseur démocrate, Joe Biden, a qualifié Dolly Parton de « figure américaine unique » qui « traitait tout le monde avec gentillesse et respect ». « Quelle merveilleuse autrice-compositrice et interprète. Elle a rassemblé tant de gens », a admiré Mick Jagger, le chanteur des Rolling Stones. L'ex-Beatles Paul McCartney a quant à lui raconté dans un post Instagram avoir rencontré Dolly Parton sur la scène mythique du Grand Ole Opry, à Nashville, au début de sa carrière. « Elle était si pétillante et pleine de vie qu'il est difficile d'accepter la nouvelle de sa disparition », a écrit le musicien britannique. Même Eminem a tenu à lui rendre hommage en publiant sur X une lettre particulièrement chaleureuse qu'elle lui avait adressée lors de son intronisation au Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. « Elle n'était vraiment pas obligée de prendre ce temps », s'est ému le rappeur américain, saluant la mémoire d'une « icône » et d'une « superstar dans tous les sens du terme ». « Tu étais le baromètre. L'étoile polaire. Audacieuse et brillante. Talentueuse et déterminée. Tu nous as tant appris sur la manière d'être soi-même, de manière unique », a de son côté salué la star américaine Beyoncé sur son site. La chanteuse Taylor Swift n'a pas été en reste, évoquant une artiste « éternellement généreuse » qui a changé « un nombre innombrable de vies » et dont l'héritage restera « éternel ». De la plume de Dolly Parton ont émergé quelque 3.000 titres, dont des classiques comme « Jolene » (1973) et « I Will Always Love You » (1974), dont la reprise en 1992 par Whitney Houston fut un succès planétaire. A New York, l’emblématique Empire State Building lui a rendu hommage en scintillant de rose dans la soirée, dès 21H25 locales, en référence à « 9 to 5 », un autre de ses tubes. The post La légende de la country Dolly Parton s’éteint à 80 ans appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: France : la surtaxe sur les bénéfices des grandes entreprises prolongée
items.description: La surtaxe sur les bénéfices des grandes entreprises devrait être reconduite en 2027, pour une troisième année consécutive, alors que le gouvernement français cherche à préserver ses recettes fiscales dans le cadre de la préparation du projet de budget pour l’année prochaine. Le ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle, énergétique et numérique, Roland Lescure, a confirmé cette orientation tout en indiquant qu’une baisse du taux de cette contribution pourrait être envisagée si la situation des finances publiques le permet, rapportent les médias locaux. Créée dans le cadre du budget 2025 comme une mesure exceptionnelle d’une durée initialement limitée à un an, cette contribution avait déjà été prolongée pour 2026. Sa reconduction en 2027 marquerait ainsi une nouvelle prolongation de ce dispositif, qui concerne environ 300 grandes entreprises réalisant au moins 1,5 milliard d’euros de chiffre d’affaires. La surtaxe devrait rapporter quelque 7,3 milliards d’euros en 2026, constituant une recette importante pour l’État dans un contexte marqué par la persistance du déficit et les efforts engagés pour redresser les comptes publics. «Si on peut la baisser, on le fera, mais aujourd’hui ce n’est pas facile », a récemment déclaré Roland Lescure aux médias laissant entendre que l’évolution du taux dépendra notamment des marges de manœuvre budgétaires disponibles. Le gouvernement français entend ainsi maintenir cette recette tout en affichant sa volonté de ne pas alourdir davantage la fiscalité des entreprises. Selon la presse, le ministre de l’Économie a notamment écarté l’idée d’une multiplication de nouvelles taxes, privilégiant une combinaison de maîtrise des dépenses et de maintien de certaines recettes existantes. Cette décision intervient alors que la préparation du projet de loi de finances pour 2027 s’annonce particulièrement délicate, sur fond de déficit public élevé et de croissance économique modérée. La Commission européenne anticipe notamment un déficit français pouvant atteindre 5,7 % du PIB en 2027 en l’absence de mesures suffisantes sur les dépenses et les recettes. La question de la fiscalité des entreprises devrait également être au cœur des échanges entre le gouvernement et le patronat à l’occasion de la Rencontre des entrepreneurs de France (REF 2026), à laquelle Roland Lescure doit participer jeudi à Paris. The post France : la surtaxe sur les bénéfices des grandes entreprises prolongée appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
